# Public /privacy and /terms pages, so Google sign-in can leave Testing

**2026-09-29, the third entry of the day.** Google keeps the OAuth consent
screen in **Testing**, where only listed test users can sign in. The free
scan now needs a Google sign-in, so no real prospect could get one. Google
will not publish the screen without a public privacy policy on an authorised
domain. The founder will enter these two URLs in Google Cloud → Branding:
`https://ai-visibility-platform-1.onrender.com/privacy` and
`https://ai-visibility-platform-1.onrender.com/terms`.

**Both pages are DRAFTS for the founder's review.** An agent that is not a
lawyer wrote them from what the code does. They should be reviewed by one
before real customers pay. The draft status is recorded here and in code
comments (`lib/legal/operator.ts`, both page components), and deliberately
not on the rendered pages.

## What the founder supplied, asked rather than guessed

- **Operator:** Priyansh Ranpura, sole trader, Melbourne, Australia, ABN
  89 415 092 182. The ABN passes the ATO's mod-89 checksum, and a test pins
  that.
- **Contact** for privacy questions and deletion requests:
  priyansh.ranpura9@gmail.com, published with the founder's say-so.
- **Redis** runs on Render Key Value. It holds sign-in sessions and, for 10
  minutes, the Google email and name of an unfinished sign-up. If it ran
  anywhere else, that host would have been a missing processor.
- **Supabase** as the database host comes from the brief. The repository
  cannot show it: `DATABASE_URL` is configuration, and the build log only ever
  lists Supabase as one candidate among four. The 2026-09-28 entry's phrase
  "the Render Postgres URL" was an assumption, and this corrects it.

No `TODO(founder)` value remains, and both pages publish on this commit.

## How the facts were established

Three read-only sweeps, each claim then spot-checked by hand:
1. every outbound host and dependency;
2. every stored column, Redis key, file and log line;
3. exactly what each provider receives.

What the pages state, in brief:

- **Stored.**
  - Account: name, email, role, last sign-in, and an Argon2id hash or
    Google's `sub`.
  - Agency: name, invitations, and a logo URL if set.
  - Clients: domain, name, brand, industry and niche, and competitors.
  - Scan facts: mentions, positions, cited URLs and domains, sentiment
    labels, and audit results.
  - Text: the questions, text an operator types into a re-run, and the
    written recommendations.
  - Billing: Stripe ids, status and period end.
  - Tokens: session, reset and invite tokens as SHA-256 digests only.
- **Not stored:** answer text or page copy. Cited as the facts-only rule
  (`test_facts_only.py` and the API-boundary tests), with its real scope: the
  facts tables cannot hold that text, and no response returns it. Also not
  stored: IP addresses and card details.
- **Processors:**
  - Render: web app, API, sessions and logs.
  - Supabase: the database.
  - Stripe: receives the agency name and id; the payer's card and email go
    to Stripe directly.
  - Google sign-in: returns `sub`, email and name.
  - Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini and Perplexity: questions only, and never
    a user's name, email or id. Checked in the prompt builder and every SDK
    call: no `user` or `metadata` field is ever sent.
  - Anthropic also receives up to three public pages of a client's site, the
    answers that name the client, and a finished scan's facts.
  - SerpApi: brand or domain and industry search terms.
  - Resend: recipient, subject and message.
  - Google Fonts: in the visitor's browser, on every page.
  - jsDelivr: only on the API's `/api/v1/docs` page.
- **Cookies:** one, `avp_session` (httpOnly, 14 days or until sign-out), plus
  two preferences in browser storage, `avp.theme` and `avp.sidebar.clients`.
  No analytics.
- **Logs:** the API's access log records IP addresses and paths, and some
  events record an email address. Render keeps them.
- **Retention:** kept while the agency uses the service, with no self-serve
  deletion. Seat removal ends sign-in but keeps the person's details. The
  expiry times are listed, and deletion is by email, done by hand.
- **Law:** the Australian Privacy Principles and the OAIC; the terms add the
  Australian Consumer Law.

## Built

- **Routes `/privacy` and `/terms`,** both prerendered as static pages in
  `next build`.
  - The route files are server components that export page titles. The
    content components are client boundaries, like every other page here.
  - Reason: the plan constants live in a `'use client'` module
    (`PricingCard`), and a server component importing a value from one gets a
    client reference, not the number.
  - Neither route calls the session API.
- **The landing page's header, shared** (`MarketingHeader`).
  - Away from the landing page it drops the section nav and links the
    wordmark home.
  - Its buttons open `/?view=sign-in` and `/?view=sign-up`. The front door
    now reads those (`lib/auth/frontDoor.ts`, cleared on arrival like the
    Google failure reason), so **Log in** on `/privacy` lands on the sign-in
    form rather than on a second landing page.
- **A footer** (`MarketingFooter`) on the landing page and both legal pages,
  linking both.
- **`PageSection` gains `headingAs`,** so each page's title is its one `h1`
  with no change of look.
- **Numbers from constants, held to the API.**
  - `PLAN_SCANS_PER_MONTH` and `PLAN_FREE_SCANS` join `PLAN_PRICE_USD` and
    `PLAN_SEATS`. The pricing card's "40" is no longer typed by hand.
  - `lib/legal/retention.ts` holds every duration the privacy page states.
  - Tests read the API's own source (`scan_allowance.py`, `config.py`,
    `share.py`, `intake.py`) and fail if a copy drifts.
- **Settings' "Not built yet" list** loses "Usage limits… there is no cap to
  hit". That has been false since the scan allowance shipped (2026-09-28),
  and the terms now state the cap.

## Found, not fixed

- **Blank keys count as set.** A blank provider key, including `RESEND_API_KEY=`
  as `.env.example` ships it, still sends the request with an empty key. The
  recipient, subject and reset link reach Resend before it is refused.
  SerpApi's call is the exception: a blank key sends nothing.
- **Reset and invite links in the logs.** With Resend unset, those links,
  with live tokens, are printed to stdout, which Render keeps.
- **DEBUG logging is always on.** structlog is never configured, so DEBUG
  lines always print, including model-written reasoning about client sites.
- **The access log records paths.** uvicorn's access log records share-link
  tokens and Google callback codes in the paths.
- **No deletion anywhere.** There is no endpoint for an account, agency,
  client or scan. A removed person's email stays reserved.
- **Public API docs.** `/api/v1/docs` is served in every environment and
  loads its viewer from jsDelivr.
- **Cancellation depends on Stripe.** Whether cancelling is enabled is a
  Stripe-dashboard portal setting the code cannot see, and the terms promise
  it.

# Live tokens out of the logs, "no email" said out loud, quieter logs, and a cancelled plan that says "Ends"

**2026-09-29, the fourth entry of the day.** Four of the findings the third
entry listed as "Found, not fixed", fixed in order of severity. The founder
confirmed the production facts today:

- `RESEND_API_KEY` is **not set** on Render.
- Google sign-in is published, and the exemption variable is set.
- `ENVIRONMENT` is `production` on the API service.
- The live Stripe webhook sends every event, `customer.subscription.updated`
  included.

**Nothing the founder does on Render changes.** The new column arrives through
the migration the container runs on start (`docker-entrypoint.sh`), and
`ENVIRONMENT=production` already makes INFO the log level. `LOG_LEVEL` stays
optional.

## 1. Live tokens never reach the logs

With Resend unset, the reset and invitation paths printed the whole link, live
token included, to stdout, and Render keeps stdout. Anyone who could read
those logs could take over any account that asked for a reset.

- **`services/email.py` logs the event, the user id and the outcome**, in
  every configuration:
  - `*.not_sent` with its reason;
  - `*.sent`;
  - `*.failed` with the error's type.

  It never logs the address, the link or the token.
- **`password_reset.request.no_account`** no longer logs the address that was
  typed.
- **A blank key is unset, for every provider key.** One normaliser in
  `config.py` (`PROVIDER_SETTINGS`) replaces the Google-only one.
  - `RESEND_API_KEY=`, as `.env.example` ships it, now sends nothing.
  - Before, it posted the recipient, the subject and the reset link to Resend
    with an empty key.
- **Nothing else logs one either.** An AST sweep of every log call in
  `apps/api/src` and `apps/workers/src` found no other event carrying an
  email address, a link or a token.

## 2. When email is off, the product says so

Resend needs a verified sending domain, and the product still runs on
`onrender.com`, so email is off in production for now.

- **Password reset.**
  - `POST /auth/reset-password/request` gains `emailConfigured`, and with it
    false the detail says no link was sent.
  - The field reports whether `RESEND_API_KEY` is set, which is the same for
    every address, so it is no enumeration oracle. Tests assert byte-identical
    bodies for an account and a stranger in both modes.
  - The screen said "Check your email… a reset link is on its way" whatever
    happened. With email off it now says "No email was sent", then the
    founder's sentence: "Password reset by email isn't available yet. Sign in
    with Google if your account uses this address, or email
    priyansh.ranpura9@gmail.com and we'll reset it by hand." It offers **Sign
    in with Google** and **Back to sign in**.
  - Signing in with Google on the same address links the password account and
    signs the person in, so that path is a complete reset.
  - The form no longer promises an email before it knows whether one can be
    sent: "Enter the address you sign in with." and **Continue**.
- **Invitations.**
  - With email off, `POST /agencies/{id}/invitations` returns the accept link
    once, in `acceptUrl`, to the owner or admin who made the invitation. With
    email on, `acceptUrl` is always null.
  - The token is still stored only as a digest. The roster never shows the
    link, and re-inviting mints a fresh one.
  - The seat screen shows the link in a read-only field with **Copy link**,
    under the line "Email isn't set up yet — send this link yourself. It works
    once and expires in 7 days."
  - As `ShareLinkBar` does, a refused clipboard leaves the link on screen to
    select.
  - Wording that implied sending is now neutral:
    - the button says **Invite**;
    - the intro reads "An invitation is a link…";
    - a re-invite with email off says "send them the new one";
    - the outstanding list says re-inviting "makes" a fresh link.
- **Privacy page:** Resend "sends password-reset and invitation emails when
  this service's email is set up".

## 3. Logs: INFO in production, and no secrets in access-log paths

- **`avp_api/logs.py`, called first in `create_app`, sets structlog's level
  once.**
  - `LOG_LEVEL` wins when set. Otherwise the level is INFO on staging and
    production, and DEBUG on local and test.
  - The two DEBUG lines that carry model-written reasoning about client sites
    (`classify.result`, `fixes.reasoning`) no longer print in production.
  - A misspelt level fails at boot.
- **The same module installs a filter on `uvicorn.access`.**
  - `/reports/{token}` and its `.pdf` log as `/reports/…`.
  - `/auth/google/callback` and `/auth/google/pending` lose their query
    strings (`code`, `state`, `ticket`).
  - Every other path is untouched.
- **The filter is installed for the process Render runs.**
  - `apps/api/docker-entrypoint.sh` execs `uvicorn avp_api.main:app`.
  - `main.py` builds `app = create_app()` on import, and `create_app` calls
    `configure_logging`.
  - uvicorn configures its own loggers in `Config.__init__`, before it
    imports the app, so nothing overwrites the filter.
  - Checked live: that command, run locally with `ENVIRONMENT=production`
    (only the host and port differ), logged `GET /api/v1/reports/…`,
    `/reports/….pdf`, `/auth/google/callback` and `/auth/google/pending`.
    None of the sentinel token, code, state, ticket or email address appeared
    anywhere in its output.
- **The privacy page's logs paragraph now matches.**
  - The secret parts of addresses are left out.
  - Events name an account by id, not email.
  - No reset or invitation link is written.
- **`.env.example`:**
  - `LOG_LEVEL` is blank, so the environment decides.
  - The Resend note no longer says the email "is logged instead".
  - `test_env_template.py` now requires the Resend key to be blank there.

## 4. A cancelled plan says "Ends", not "Renews"

Stripe's portal cancels at the end of the period, and until then the
subscription stays `active` with `cancel_at_period_end: true`.

- **The column.** `agencies.subscription_cancel_at_period_end` is a boolean,
  not null, default false (migration `55c6b4395e7d`).
  - Existing rows are backfilled to false. A subscription cancelled in the
    portal before this deploy reads false until Stripe's next update for it.
    Resending that event from the Stripe dashboard corrects it.
  - **The server default is kept**, unlike `competitors.corroborated`'s. The
    container migrates before it serves, so the old instance keeps serving
    during a deploy, and its sign-ups insert agencies without this column.
    The model declares the same default, so `alembic check` stays clean.
  - The first draft dropped the default, and a review before the commit
    caught that. An insert that omits the column, run against `avp_dev` in a
    rolled-back transaction, now gets false.
- **The webhook** stores it from `customer.subscription.created` and
  `.updated`, and `.deleted` sets it false.
- **The API.** `GET /agencies/{id}/billing` gains `cancelAtPeriodEnd`.
- **The screen.** BillingPanel shows "Ends {date}" and "Cancelled — you keep
  full access until then, and it won't renew." **Manage billing** stays, so
  the plan can be resumed.
- **The allowance is unchanged.** The status stays `active`, so the plan's 40
  scans a month apply until the period ends, and a test pins this.

- **Still open from the third entry:**

# Citation Strength repeated Mention Rate — measured at ρ 0.781, so v5 asks how a brand is backed when it is named

**2026-09-29, the fifth entry of the day.** Since v4 both dimensions read the
same population, awareness answers. Citation Strength summed the authority of
every tiered domain cited in the awareness answers that named a brand, so a
brand named in more of them collected more citations almost mechanically. If
the two moved together, the composite counted one fact twice, at 30 + 20 =
50% of its weight. The brief fixed a decision rule before any number was
seen: Spearman ρ with zeros excluded ≥ 0.70 means the overlap is real, and
v5 follows. Under 0.70, keep v4. Under 15 pairs, too little data.

## 1. Measured, before anything changed

**Method.** `scripts/measure_citation_overlap.py`, committed so the figure
can be re-run as scans accumulate:

- It scores every scan with a Score row with `score_scan(persist=False)`, the
  same 26 scans the v4 entry measured. `avp_dev` has nothing newer than
  2026-09-12.
- It collects (Mention Rate, Citation Strength) for the subject and for every
  rival in the comparison.
- Rivals carry a figure only when the subject's is included, so 22 scans
  contribute pairs: 22 subject pairs and 110 rival pairs.
- The per-scan values reproduce the v4 entry's table exactly, so the lookup
  and the data are the ones v4 was measured on.
- ρ was checked against an independent average-rank implementation, and the
  two agree to four places.

**Under v4:**

| | n | Pearson r | Spearman ρ |
|---|---|---|---|
| all pairs | 132 | 0.872 | 0.880 |
| zeros excluded | **83** | 0.747 | **0.781** |

The scatter is `docs/screenshots/citation-overlap-2026-09-29/overlap-v4.png`
(hand-written SVG rendered by Playwright; there is no matplotlib in the API
venv). Hollow marks are the pairs with a zero.

**Where the two sub-scores differed most under v4,** one row per brand. These
are the cases where Citation Strength carried its own information:

| brand | scan of | Mention Rate | Citation Strength |
|---|---|---|---|
| Freshdesk (rival) | helpwise.io | 75.00 | 0.00 |
| Seline (rival) | plausible.io | 8.33 | 70.00 |
| PostHog (rival) | plausible.io | 39.39 | 100.00 |
| Missive (rival) | front.com | 50.00 | 100.00 |
| Zendesk (rival) | helpscout.com | 50.00 | 0.00 |

**Verdict: ρ = 0.781 with zeros excluded, n = 83. That is at least 0.70 and
above the 15-pair minimum, so the overlap is real and section 2 ran.**

## 2. v5: Citation Strength conditional on being named

**The measure now asks "when an engine names you, does it back you with
authoritative sources?"**

- For each awareness answer that names a brand, the answer's authority sum is
  the `AUTHORITY_VALUES` of the distinct third-party domains it cites, less
  the brand's own domain.
- The brand's raw value is the **mean** of those sums over the answers that
  name it.
- The subject is normalised against the best mean in the scan, as v4 did.

`authority_sums` became `authority_when_named`, because what it returns
changed from a sum to a mean.

**Unchanged:**
- the tiers, `AUTHORITY_VALUES` and co-occurrence attribution;
- the normalisation;
- the weights;
- the three scan-level exclusions and their order.

A brand named in no awareness answer scores 0 and is not excluded, subject
or rival. Excluding it would move its 20% to the other dimensions and could
raise an invisible brand's composite, and a test shows exactly that.

`FORMULA_VERSION = "v5"`, a major bump because it redefines a weighted
dimension. scoring-spec.md has a new v5 section, the edge-case row and a
changelog row with the reason and the measured ρ. **Stored v4 rows are not
re-scored.**

**Re-measured under v5:** zeros excluded, n = 83, r = 0.215, **ρ = 0.177**.
Over all pairs r = 0.695 and ρ = 0.708, because the zero pairs still line up
by construction. The change counts only if ρ falls below 0.70, and it did.
The formula was not tuned. The scatter is `overlap-v5.png`.

## Found, not fixed: a mean lets a rarely named rival set the scale

The best mean in a scan can belong to a brand named in only a handful of
answers. Where each scan's best comes from:

- **Seline, named in 3 of 36 awareness answers,** holds a mean of 116.67 on
  plausible.io `VRNNXXB1`. Plausible Analytics is named in all 36 with a mean
  of 20.83, which is why it reads 17.86.
- **Freshworks (Freshdesk), named in 4 of 35,** sets intercom.com's scale.
- No scan's best is set by a brand named only once. Elsewhere the best is
  named in 6 to 45 answers, or is the subject itself.

This is the property the brief asked for: a brand named twice and backed
both times outscores one named eight times and backed once. It also means the
scale can rest on few answers. A floor on how many answers a brand needs
before its mean can set the scale would be a formula change of its own. The
brief said not to tune toward the threshold, so it is not made here.

# A rarely named brand still sets Citation Strength's scale: shrinkage (v6) measured and rejected, and a 45-word note

**2026-09-29, the sixth entry of the day.** The v5 entry flagged a property
of a plain mean. A rival named in a handful of awareness answers can hold a
scan's best mean, and every other brand is normalised against it. On one
plausible.io scan, Seline, named in 3 of 36 answers, marked Plausible
Analytics, named in all 36, down to 17.86. The brief fixed a candidate and a
rule before anything was measured.

## What was tried (v6)

Each brand's per-answer mean is shrunk toward the scan's pooled mean P:
`(sum of the brand's answer sums + K × P) / (n + K)`, with **K = 3**.

- **n** is the number of awareness answers that name the brand.
- **P** is the mean authority over every (answer, named brand) pair among
  the brands compared.
- A brand named in no answer stays at 0, not P.
- Everything else was v5's.

**The rule.** Ship only if ρ against Mention Rate (zeros excluded) stays
below 0.70, **and** fewer scans have a scale set by a brand named in fewer
than 5 answers than under v5. Keep v5 if n (zeros excluded) is under 15.

**The measurement.**
- `scripts/measure_citation_overlap.py` now also reports, per scan, which
  brand sets the scale and how many awareness answers name it. Ties are
  held jointly, so a scan counts as small-sample only if every brand at the
  top is.
- It ran on v5, then on v6 implemented in `scoring.py`, over the same 26
  scored scans.
- v6's arithmetic was checked by hand against the implementation on the two
  scans where a rival sets the scale, and matched exactly.

| | ρ, zeros excluded | n | ρ, all 132 pairs | scale set by a brand named < 5 times |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v5 | 0.177 | 83 | 0.708 | 3 of 19 |
| v6 | 0.301 | 95 | 0.715 | 3 of 19 |

Every scan's scale-setter was the same brand under both:

| client | scan | sets the scale (v5 and v6 alike) | named in | under 5? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| helpscout.com | `0NC3SV8W` | Help Scout and Front | 2 and 2 | **yes** |
| basecamp.com | `DD12YYE0` | Teamwork | 8 | no |
| linear.app | `XVJ77KSS` | Shortcut | 23 | no |
| plausible.io | `VRNNXXB1` | Seline | 3 | **yes** |
| plausible.io | `1YDNFAAM` | PostHog | 18 | no |
| plausible.io | `BZ9EY9QM` | PostHog | 13 | no |
| notion.so | `AX2PBBB9` | Airtable | 12 | no |
| notion.so | `P8A075RZ` | ClickUp | 15 | no |
| front.com | `W0JRMC9E` | Missive | 6 | no |
| missiveapp.com | `8ADTZ6ZT` | Gmelius | 6 | no |
| zammad.com | `58RXESN4` | Zendesk | 8 | no |
| helpwise.io | `QM1ATB7R` | Missive | 8 | no |
| pirsch.io | `H84RKKH2` | Plausible Analytics | 36 | no |
| helpwise.io | `Z82H0P59` | Missive | 6 | no |
| intercom.com | `QT7WMVXZ` | Freshworks (Freshdesk) | 4 | **yes** |
| helpwise.io | `34MJCNZ1` | Freshdesk | 28 | no |
| hiverhq.com | `V7DEYSE5` | Hiver | 39 | no |
| groovehq.com | `GEAFNQ8H` | Zendesk | 45 | no |
| reamaze.com | `6H6C00ME` | Freshdesk | 24 | no |

The three remaining scans with Citation Strength included (psmdigitalagency.com
and psmdigitalagency.com.au twice) back no brand at all under either formula.

## Verdict: v6 rejected, v5 stands

The ρ guard held, and the count did not fall, so v6 does not ship.
`FORMULA_VERSION` stays `v5`, and nothing is re-scored. K was not tuned.

**Why shrinkage could not fix it.** A very high mean over three answers
survives being blended with three answers' worth of the average:

- **plausible.io** (P = 26.05 over 119 pairs): Seline goes from 116.67 to
  71.36, still far above Matomo, the next brand, at 28.01 (named in 23).
- **intercom.com** (P = 27.69 over 65 pairs): Freshworks goes from 50.00 to
  40.44, still above Zendesk at 28.49 and the subject at 27.60.
- **helpscout.com** has only two awareness answers, so no averaging rule can
  give it a scale-setter named five times.

Shrinkage also lifts a brand whose naming answers cite nothing trusted
toward P. Botpress, named in 4 answers with nothing tiered, went from 0 to
11.87, which is why n rose from 83 to 95.

**The property stays open.** What would close it — a minimum number of
answers before a brand can set the scale, or another treatment of small
samples — is a formula decision of its own. scoring-spec.md records all of
this under v5, as "Small-n measured, v6 rejected (2026-09-29)".

**A reading of the brief, moot because v6 did not ship.** The brief said
that when P is 0, `NO_AUTHORITY_DATA` "applies as today". Today that code
fires only when no awareness answer cites anything tiered. The three
psmdigitalagency scans are a third case: tiered sources are cited, but only
in answers that name no brand. They score 0 and stay included. The v6
implementation left that unchanged. Excluding them would have raised three
unnamed brands' composites, and made the exclusion copy's "nothing cited …
is on either tier" untrue.

**Left in the code.**
- `answer_authority`, split out of `authority_when_named`, returns each
  brand's per-answer sums. It is behaviour-neutral: the final run
  reproduces the v5 run pair for pair. Two tests pin it: the value is
  exactly the plain mean of the lists, and a brand named in no answer gets
  an empty list and a 0.
- A rejection note on `authority_when_named`, and one line by
  `FORMULA_VERSION`.
- The script's scale-setter report.

## The client-facing note: 45 words

`DIMENSION_NOTE` for Citation Strength, on both sides of the language
boundary, now reads:

> When AI names the brand, how often does it back it with a trusted source?
> It counts only answers to questions that did not name the brand. Some
> sources qualify as trusted through uncalibrated industry labels — a coarse
> proxy that a mis-classified client can skew.

**45 words**, counting whitespace-separated tokens that contain a letter or
digit (the dash is not a word). The v5 note had 239.

**What stayed.** "uncalibrated", "coarse proxy" and "mis-classified" stay,
because the copy contract requires them in this note.
- When the dimension is measured, this note is the only place the proxy's
  limit reaches a reader.
- The report has no general caveat or method section they could move to.
- The `NO_AUTHORITY_DATA` exclusion detail carries them, but only when the
  dimension is left out.
- "only answers to questions that did not name the brand" also stays, because
  it changes how the number reads.

**What left.** The tier list and the market-participant rule. They remain in
the `NO_AUTHORITY_DATA` detail and in scoring-spec.md. The contract's
"brands in a scanned market" check now applies to the exclusion detail
only.

**Contract checks.** New tests on both sides hold the note to 45 words and
to your question. `report-copy.json` was regenerated with
`AVP_WRITE_FIXTURES=1`, a one-line change, and `copyContract.test.ts` and
`test_report_copy.py` pass. No wording about shrinkage was added, since v6
did not ship.

**Screenshots,** in `docs/screenshots/citation-note-2026-09-29/`:
- `report-note-light-1280.png` and `report-note-dark-1280.png` show the real
  `ReportView` in the route frame. The report is paper in both themes, so
  only the page around it differs.
- `report-note-pdf-page1.png` is page 1 of a real `render_report_pdf`
  output, rasterised with Quick Look. The note prints under the score
  table.
- Both use the shared Help Scout case, marked v5 with its pre-v2.1
  degradation flag removed, so the page shows no stale caveat. The numbers
  are unchanged.

## Verified

- **API 1557 → 1560** (+3: the two `answer_authority` tests and the Python
  word-limit test).
- **Web 997 → 998** (+1: the TypeScript word-limit test).
- `ReportView.test.tsx` and the PDF test pin the new wording.
- Workers 13, shared-types 53, and the full design-system suite at 649.
- ruff clean; mypy 47 under its 50 ceiling.
- All three typechecks clean.
- All six count gates through `assert_count.py`.
- Both `uv lock --check` runs pass.

# Four loose ends before real customers: a manual reset, closed API docs, the crawler page, and the web's own logs

**2026-09-29, the seventh entry of the day.** Four items, ordered by how
likely each was to bite a paying customer. One commit.

**Nothing to set on Render.** The crawler's address is built from
`PUBLIC_WEB_BASE_URL`, which on the API service is already
`https://ai-visibility-platform-1.onrender.com` (the Epic 20 live probe saw
Google's callback redirect there). The docs close on the `ENVIRONMENT=production`
the service already has.

## 1. A manual password reset

`apps/api/scripts/issue_password_reset.py --email <address>` is the "we'll
reset it by hand" the forgot-password screen promises.

- **One token path.** It mints through `password_reset.request_reset`, the
  function the forgot-password route calls. So the storage is digest-only,
  the expiry is `password_reset_ttl_seconds`, and earlier links are retired.
  The link comes from the new `password_reset.reset_url`, which the route's
  email now uses too, so the two cannot build different links.
- **Output.** It prints the link once, to its own stdout. No log line carries
  the link, the token or the address. The service's own
  `password_reset.request.minted` line names the account by user id.
- **Refusals.**
  - Unknown or deleted address: "No such user.", exit 1. Only someone with a
    shell on the API service can ask, so saying so is no enumeration oracle.
  - Suspended, or invited and never joined: exit 2.
  - No password: exit 2, "They should use Sign in with Google". The users
    table's check constraint makes an active account with no password a
    Google account. A link would ADD a password to an account that never had
    one.
- **Its own engine,** disposed at exit, and the API's logging configuration.
- **`docs/runbook.md` (new)** has the Render-shell command, what each outcome
  prints, and what to do with the link: send it to the account's own
  address.
- **Not run inside the image,** because this machine has no Docker. The
  command's paths come from the Dockerfile: `WORKDIR /app`, the venv at
  `/app/apps/api/.venv`, and `scripts/` inside the build context
  (`.dockerignore` keeps all of `apps/api`). The same invocation,
  `.venv/bin/python scripts/issue_password_reset.py`, ran locally against
  `avp_dev` and printed "No such user." with exit 1.

## 2. The API's docs are closed where it is deployed

- **`create_app`:** in staging and production, `docs_url` and `openapi_url`
  are `None`. `redoc_url` was already `None` everywhere. Local and test are
  unchanged.
- **Nothing deployed reads them.**
  - The web app uses the committed `api.gen.ts`.
  - The Dockerfile's HEALTHCHECK calls `/health`; CI's image job calls
    `/health` and `/ready`.
  - The workers never call the API over HTTP.
- **The export still works.** `scripts/export_openapi.py` builds the app with
  `Settings(environment="local")` and calls `app.openapi()`, which needs no
  URL. It was run plainly, then with `ENVIRONMENT=production` plus a
  real-shaped `APP_SECRET` and CORS origin. Both exited 0, and both outputs
  are byte-identical to the committed `openapi.json`.
  - With `ENVIRONMENT=production` and nothing else it fails at import: the
    module-level `app = create_app()` refuses the placeholder secret. That
    was true before this change, and CI never sets the variable.
- **jsDelivr leaves the privacy page** and the provider fixture. It served
  only the docs page's viewer.
- The README says the docs are local and test only.

## 3. The crawler page

**Traced in the code before a word was written:**

- **Which sites.** Only a site an agency has added as a client. Competitors
  are found through SerpApi and engine answers, never crawled.
- **Adding a site** (and "re-classify"): `crawl_site` loads the homepage,
  then up to 2 more pages on the same host, chosen from links whose paths
  start with `CANDIDATE_PATHS`. That is at most 3 pages (`intake.py`'s
  `max_pages`). Images, fonts and video are blocked at the router.
- **Each scan** (and a manual audit re-run): `GET /robots.txt`, then
  `GET /sitemap.xml` unless robots.txt mentions a sitemap, then one full load
  of the homepage. If `load` times out, it tries once more at
  `domcontentloaded`.
- **How often.** There is no schedule anywhere: no Celery beat, and no loop in
  the API. Every run starts from a person's action.
- **robots.txt is NOT honoured.**
  - The audit fetches it only to report on it (Technical Foundation and the
    AI crawler screen).
  - Nothing consults it before a fetch, and `crawl.py` never reads it.
  - The page says so plainly, and a tripwire test fails the day either
    fetcher starts to consult it. Adding support was outside this pass.

**The user agent.** `crawl.py` holds `USER_AGENT_TEMPLATE` and
`CRAWLER_INFO_PATH`. `crawler_user_agent()` fills the template from
`PUBLIC_WEB_BASE_URL`. The crawl, the audit's browser and both side fetches
send it. In production it reads:
`Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; AVPScanBot/0.1; +https://ai-visibility-platform-1.onrender.com/crawler) Playwright/Chromium`.

**The page.**
- `/crawler` uses the privacy and terms layout, and the footer on every
  public page now links it. The privacy page links it too.
- **Rendered per request.** The web app has no setting that holds its own
  address, so the page prints the user agent with the address it was
  requested at: `x-forwarded-host`/`-proto` if present, otherwise `Host`.
  The API refuses exactly this for links. It is safe here because the
  address is printed back only to the person whose request supplied it, and
  the response is `private, no-store`.
- **"The same string", across two languages.** The web test reads both
  constants out of `crawl.py` and compares them with
  `lib/legal/crawler.ts`. It also checks the rendered page's string against
  the Python template filled with the same origin. The Python test replaces
  Playwright and httpx with recorders and captures the user agent each
  fetcher actually sends.
- **Every other fact on the page** is read back from the API's source in
  the same way. Page count, paths, side files, one page per scan, and no
  schedule are each tested.

**No placeholder left.** No `.invalid` host remains anywhere in `apps/`, and
a tree-wide test holds that. Besides the user agent, two test-data values
moved to `.example`: a web fixture's `urlAudited`, and
`verify_google_live.py`'s probe redirect URL. No new host entered the
scanned source, so the provider fixture only lost entries:
`example.invalid` and jsDelivr.

## 4. The web's own logs, and the Referer

- **`next start` prints no request lines,** so there is nothing to redact.
  - In Next 15.5.23, `logRequests` is required only by
    `server/dev/next-dev-server.js`.
  - A production build served by `next start` answered 8 requests without
    writing a byte: four token routes with sentinel tokens, `/crawler`,
    `/privacy`, a query-string variant and a 404. The log was 145 bytes
    before and after, with 0 sentinel hits.
  - The web package's `start` script is `next start`. The repo holds no
    Render configuration, so that Render runs it is an assumption.
- **The limit.** Render's own HTTP request log records every request's path,
  for both services, and the app cannot change that. On the web:
  `/share/{token}`, `/reset-password/{token}`, `/invite/{token}` and
  `/sign-up/google?ticket=`. On the API: `/api/v1/reports/{token}`.
  - The privacy page's logs paragraph said the log "cannot be used to open a
    report", and read as the whole story. A second paragraph now says
    Render keeps its own record, with full addresses, including an opened
    reset or invitation link, and that the web app keeps none.
- **Referrer-Policy.** `next.config.mjs` sends `no-referrer` on
  `/share/:token`, `/reset-password/:token`, `/invite/:token` and
  `/sign-up/google`. curl against the built server shows it on all four,
  and not on other pages.
  - The report's source links already carried `rel="noreferrer"`. The header
    adds the agency's logo, the fonts, and any future link.
  - It matters for older browsers, whose default policy sends the full
    address to HTTPS hosts. Nothing reads a Referer: the API's CORS reads
    Origin.

## Found, not fixed

- **Live tokens in Render's request log.**
  - A reset link opened but not used stays redeemable for an hour, an
    invitation for 7 days, and a share link for 30.
  - Each sits in that log with its path. Moving the web routes' token into
    the URL fragment (`#…`, never sent to a server) would close it for those
    three routes.
  - The share page's API call would still carry its token in a path.
  - Worth doing before email goes on.
- **The public reset route mints a token for a Google-only account.** A reset
  can then add a password to it. With email off nothing is sent. The script
  refuses the case; the route is unchanged.
- **`export_openapi.py`'s last line** raises `relative_to` when given an
  output path outside the repository. The file is written first, so it is
  harmless, but the run exits 1.
- **Still open:** there is no deletion endpoint.

## Verified

**API 1560 → 1575 (+15).**
- The manual reset (6):
  - the printed link, from the real command in a subprocess, is accepted by
    `reset-password/confirm`, and the new password signs in;
  - the token comes from `request_reset`, with the route's digest and expiry;
  - log capture over structlog, stdout and stdlib logging finds no token,
    link or address, and the link reaches stdout once;
  - an unknown address exits 1 from the real command;
  - Google-only and suspended accounts are refused, with no token row
    written.
- The user agent (5): built from the setting, a new domain follows it, and
  the crawl, the audit's browser and both side fetches send it.
- The docs (4): 404 for all three paths in staging and production, and
  served in local and test.

**Web 998 → 1017 (+19).**
- `crawlerPage.test.tsx` (14);
- `referrerPolicy.test.ts` (6), which finds the `[token]` routes on disk;
- the mounted `/crawler` route, signed out (1);
- minus 2 in `providers.test.ts`, whose per-provider tests for jsDelivr went
  with it.

**Negative controls, each file restored byte-for-byte:**
- a structlog call carrying the link, added to the script: the log-capture
  test fails, and so does the subprocess test (the token is printed twice);
- docs served in every environment: both deployed-docs tests fail;
- the web's template drifting from `crawl.py`, and `crawl.py`'s from the
  web: 2 tests fail each way;
- a `.invalid` URL added in `apps/api/scripts`: the tree-wide test fails;
- `/share/:token` dropped from the header rule: 2 tests fail;
- the audit returning early when robots.txt disallows: the tripwire fails;
- the crawler's host hard-coded: "a new domain moves it" fails.

**The rest of the bar.**
- Workers 13, shared-types 53, and the full design-system suite at 649.
- ruff clean (src and tests, and the new script); mypy 47, under its 50
  ceiling.
- All three typechecks clean.
- All six count gates through `assert_count.py`.
- Both `uv lock --check` runs pass.
- `next build` passes from a copy, with `/crawler` dynamic.
- Exit codes read from files.

**Screenshots,** in `docs/screenshots/crawler-page-2026-09-29/`: `/crawler`
in light and dark at 1280 and 390, from the production build.
- Served with the forwarded headers Render's proxy sends, so the user agent
  shows the production address.
- No horizontal scroll at 390 (`scrollWidth` 390).
- The user-agent block wraps to 4 lines at 1280 and 6 at 390.


# The crawler obeys robots.txt, and a public reset never adds a password to a Google-only account

**2026-09-29, the eighth entry of the day.** Two items, one commit.

**Nothing to set on Render.** No migration, no new setting, and the API
contract regenerates byte-identically.

**What an agency sees when a prospect's site blocks the crawler:**
- **On adding the site:** the client is created unclassified ("Could not
  read", reason `ROBOTS_DISALLOWED`). No page is fetched.
- **On scanning it:** the scan runs, because the engines never visit the site.
  The report leaves Technical Foundation out with "This site’s robots.txt asks
  crawlers like ours not to load its pages, so its technical foundation wasn’t
  measured." A blanket `Disallow: /` under `*` is still listed as a fix.

## 1. robots.txt, obeyed

**The rule, as the brief decided it.**
- robots.txt is always fetched first, now by the intake crawl too.
- The group naming `AVPScanBot` applies, case-insensitively; otherwise `*`.
- Longest match decides between Allow and Disallow, and Allow wins a tie.
- Every page is checked before it is requested: the homepage, the linked
  pages and `/sitemap.xml`.
- A page's own subresources are not checked, and Crawl-delay is ignored. The
  `/crawler` page says both.

**One reader.** `ai_crawlers.crawl_policy` reuses the RFC 9309 parser that
already fed the AI crawler screen: `_parse_groups`, and the longest-match
rule, moved into `_allows_rules` with no change in behaviour. Groups that name
the same agent are combined, as the RFC says.

**How a fetch's status is read** (`PolicyBasis`):
- **2xx:** the body is parsed, whatever its content type. The RFC says so,
  and a single-page app that answers `/robots.txt` with its HTML page has no
  groups, so everything is allowed.
- **Any 4xx:** there is no file, so everything is allowed. The brief named
  404 and 410. The RFC puts every 4xx here, 403 included, and so does this.
- **429:** treated like a 5xx. This is the one choice made here, since the
  RFC files 429 with the other 4xx. A site asking us to slow down is not one
  to read that minute.
- **5xx, a timeout, no answer, or too many redirects:** nothing is fetched
  from the site that run.

**The gate, `crawl.RobotsGate`.**
- It fetches each host's robots.txt once, and every page is checked before
  it is requested.
- **Redirects are followed by the gate, by hand.** A probe on 2026-09-29
  showed that Playwright's request routing never sees a redirect's second
  request. So a browser handed `https://domain` would load the www host
  before anyone read www's robots.txt.
  - The gate follows the homepage's redirects with HEAD requests, checking
    each hop's own host first.
  - The browser is then handed the resolved address.
  - Where the browser actually lands is checked too. A script's redirect, or
    one only a browser is given, is caught there, and nothing from a
    disallowed page is kept.
- The gate opens an HTTP client per call, so it can be asked from inside a
  browser session without holding a connection open around it.

**Intake.**
- **A disallowed homepage** means no browser and not even a HEAD request.
  `crawl_site` returns `ROBOTS_DISALLOWED`, and the classifier's existing
  "could not classify" path records it as the reason. The client is still
  created.
- **A disallowed candidate page** is skipped without taking a slot, so the
  next allowed candidate is read instead. A page that fails to load still
  takes its slot, as it always has.
- **The intake screen is unchanged, and the brief's sentence was not added.**
  No operator can set an industry by hand: there is no PUT or PATCH on
  clients, and no UI for it.
  - The screen still reads "We could not read this site … This usually means
    the site did not load", with "Reason: ROBOTS_DISALLOWED" under it.
  - The scan API does not require a classification, so the dashboard can
    still scan such a client, with no industry seed.

**The audit.**
- **Stored as `status=failed`, `error_code=ROBOTS_DISALLOWED`.** That needs
  no migration and no enum change. Every consumer already treats a failed
  audit as unmeasured, which is exactly what excluding Technical Foundation
  needs.
- **The checks.**
  - A blanket `Disallow: /` under `*` is known from the file alone, so it
    stays `indexable: fail` with `ROBOTS_TXT_DISALLOW`, a finding and a fix.
  - A block on AVPScanBot alone makes `indexable` `not_applicable`.
  - `robots_txt_present`, the sitemap named in robots.txt, and the AI crawler
    table are all recorded.
  - Every check that needs the page is `not_applicable` with
    `ROBOTS_DISALLOWED`. INP keeps its own code, because it can never be
    measured.
- **A disallowed `/sitemap.xml`** is not fetched, and its check is
  `not_applicable` rather than the `NO_SITEMAP_XML` finding.
  - The indexation component still counts that sitemap as absent, as it
    always has counted one it could not fetch.
  - This affects only a site that allows its homepage but forbids its
    sitemap.

**Scoring, rule 5 held.**
- The scorer already excluded Technical Foundation whenever it received
  None, and spread its weight across the others.
  - `compute_score` now also takes `technical_foundation_exclusion`, and
    `load_technical_foundation` returns `CRAWL_DISALLOWED` for a
    `ROBOTS_DISALLOWED` audit.
  - The composite is the same one an unmeasured dimension gives. That is
    tested on synthetic results, and again by re-scoring the end-to-end
    scan's own rows.
  - `FORMULA_VERSION` stays v5.
- **The `TECHNICAL_FOUNDATION_NOT_MEASURED` flag is not raised.** Its
  sentence, "had not been audited", would be false.
- **The digest.** The reason enters it only when set, so every existing
  digest is byte-identical, and a test checks that.
- **"A new flag, `CRAWL_DISALLOWED`"** was read as the exclusion reason, and
  no degradation flag was added. The report prints an exclusion's sentence
  and then the flags, so a flag would print the same sentence twice.

**Copy, on both sides.**
- `EXCLUSION_REASON.CRAWL_DISALLOWED`: the label is "Blocked by robots.txt",
  and the detail is the brief's sentence.
- `report-copy.json` was regenerated with `AVP_WRITE_FIXTURES=1`, adding one
  entry, and `copyCoverage.test.ts` lists the new code.
- **The report's audit section** reads "What the site’s robots.txt says",
  with the badge, and still shows the checks that did not pass.
- **The Technical screen** has its own wording, "This site asks crawlers
  like ours to stay out". It no longer says "could not be read".
- `fix_generator` treats `CRAWL_DISALLOWED` like `NOT_YET_MEASURED`: no gap
  fix is written for it.

**`/crawler`.**
- It now says the crawler obeys robots.txt, with the 4xx, 5xx and 429 rules,
  redirects, a page's own files, and Crawl-delay.
- It has an example to paste: `User-agent: AVPScanBot` / `Disallow: /`.
- **The tripwire is flipped.** It now requires, in the API's own source, a
  robots check before each fetch: in the gate's `follow`, before `_crawl`,
  before each candidate, after the homepage lands, and before the audit's
  browser. The browser may never be handed `start_url`.
- `CRAWLER_TOKEN`, `ROBOTS_DISALLOWED` and the status rules are read back
  from the Python source.

## 2. The public reset form never mints for an account without a password

- **`request_reset`** treats `password_hash IS NULL` like "no account". It
  logs `password_reset.request.no_password` by user id, mints nothing, and
  returns None.
- **The reply is byte-identical** to an unknown address's, and a test
  compares the bytes. The existing identical-body tests pass untouched.
- **The operator script is unchanged.** It still checks before calling
  `request_reset`, so its message stays the clearer one.

## Live check

**No `avp_dev` client blocks `/` outright.**
- groovehq.com is the only one the Epic 6 reader flags. Its file reads
  `User-agent: *`, `Disallow: /`, `Allow: /$`, so by longest match its
  homepage is allowed.
- **Run live through the real `audit_site`, with real Chromium:**
  - robots.txt came first.
  - `/sitemap.xml` was not requested.
  - The homepage redirects twice, from groovehq.com to www.groovehq.com to
    helply.com. Each host's robots.txt was read before its HEAD request.
  - The browser was handed `https://helply.com/`, and the audit scored
    68.00.
  - The intake crawl, run live too, read helply.com's homepage and `/about`.
- **So the blocked path ran against a local server** serving
  `User-agent: *` / `Disallow: /`, through the real `audit_site` and
  `crawl_site` with Chromium installed.
  - The server's own log shows only `GET /robots.txt`, once per crawler.
  - No browser launched, and both returned `ROBOTS_DISALLOWED`.
  - The audit recorded the robots facts and the blanket finding, and was not
    scored.

## Found, not fixed

- **The Technical screen shows every `partial` audit as "The site could not
  be read".** 8 of the 25 audits in `avp_dev` are `partial` (a component had
  no signal, usually the date), and all 8 are scored.
  `routers/audits.py` also computes components only for `ok`.
- **The Epic 6 blanket reader and the RFC parser disagree on groovehq.com.**
  The old reader sees `Disallow: /` and ignores `Allow: /$`. So `indexable`
  fails with `ROBOTS_TXT_DISALLOW`, while the crawler, obeying the same file,
  loads the homepage. It is a scored input, left alone as Epic F decided,
  but the contradiction is now visible.
- **The robots facts come from the host a scan starts at**, while the page
  audited can be on another host after redirects (groovehq.com → helply.com).
  That was already so before this change.
- **The AI crawler table's `_select_group` still takes the first matching
  group** where the RFC combines them. The crawler's own policy combines.
- **No operator can set an industry by hand**, so a blocked prospect stays
  unclassified.

## Verified

**API 1575 → 1620 (+45).**
- `test_robots_obeyed.py` (41):
  - the parser rules;
  - the gate: once per host, a disallowed redirect never requested, an
    allowed one resolved with HEAD, a timeout;
  - intake: a disallowed homepage fetches nothing, the client is created
    with the reason, a candidate is skipped without taking a slot, and a
    landing elsewhere is checked; 404 and 410 crawl, 503 does not;
  - the audit: no browser, the robots facts, the blanket finding, a block on
    AVPScanBot alone, a disallowed sitemap not fetched and an allowed one
    fetched;
  - the composite equals the excluded composite and not a zero, the digests
    are unchanged, and an unknown reason is refused.
- One end-to-end chain test: a real scan through the real `audit_site`
  against a site blocking `*`. It checks the audit row, `CRAWL_DISALLOWED`
  on the score, a re-score with the dimension excluded that gives the same
  composite, and the report.
- The reset (3): a byte-identical reply, no token and no address logged, and
  a password account still gets one.
- The UA tests were rewritten on the fake web, and now cover the HEAD hop.

**Web 1017 → 1023 (+6).**
- `/crawler`: the policy, the required checks, and the reason code (3
  replacing 1);
- the report's blocked audit (3);
- copy coverage (1).

**Negative control.** With the audit's check before the homepage removed,
both homepage-disallowed audit tests fail. The file was restored
byte-for-byte.

**The rest of the bar.**
- Workers 13, shared-types 53, and the full design-system suite at 649.
- ruff clean; mypy 47, under its 50 ceiling.
- All three typechecks clean.
- All six count gates through `assert_count.py`.
- Both `uv lock --check` runs pass.

- Exit codes read from files.

**Screenshots,** in `docs/screenshots/robots-obeyed-2026-09-29/`.

  390.
- The report's exclusion note and its robots.txt audit section, from the
  production build's `/share` page with the API answered from the new

# Share, invite and reset tokens leave the URL path

**2026-09-30, the first entry of the day.** One item, one commit.

**Nothing to set on Render.** No migration and no new setting. The API and web
deploy from the same push. For the minute between the two deploys, a web page
still calling the old GET gets a 404, and a reload fixes it.

## 1. What changes for a person

- **Links sent from now on** read `/share#…`, `/invite#…` and `/reset-password#…`.
  The part after `#` is never sent to any server, so it cannot reach Render's
  request log, the API's log, or a Referer.
- **Links already sent** (`/share/<token>` and so on) still work: the old page
  loads, sends the browser to the `#` form with `location.replace`, and offers
  an "Open the link" anchor, plus a `<noscript>` note for a visitor without
  JavaScript.
- **The share page keeps its `#…` in the address bar**, so a report can be
  reloaded, bookmarked and forwarded. It also reacts to a pasted `#` change in
  the same tab.
- **Invite and reset remove it once read** (`history.replaceState(null, …)`),
  because they are single-use secrets. A reload afterwards says: "This page no
  longer has the link's code (it is removed from the address bar once read).
  Open the link from your email again."

## 2. The mechanism

- **`apps/api/src/avp_api/services/links.py`** is now the one place link shapes
  are built (`share_link`, `invite_link`, `reset_link`). It is used by
  `_share_url`, the seat invitation, `reset_url` and `scripts/issue_password_reset.py`.
- **`GET /reports/{token}` and `GET /reports/{token}.pdf` are replaced** by
  `POST /reports/shared` and `POST /reports/shared/pdf` with the token in the
  body.
- **`logs.py` still redacts** any legacy `/reports/<token>` path. It now logs
  exactly `/reports/shared` and `/reports/shared/pdf` as they are, and redacts
  every other remainder and any query string under `/reports/`.
- **The web reads the token** through `src/lib/fragmentToken.ts`. The first
  render is a neutral loading state, so there is no hydration mismatch and no
  error flash, and an empty fragment goes straight to the invalid state.
- **The public PDF is a POST** that returns a Blob, saved through
  `DownloadPdfButton`. It now keeps focus while busy (`aria-disabled`), has a
  visually hidden status ("Preparing the PDF…", then "PDF downloaded"), and its
  error is tied to the button with `aria-describedby`.
- **`Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`** is on the three old routes and the three new ones.

## 3. Reviews

- **The security review found no Critical, High or Medium issue.**
- **Its Lows were fixed:**
  - Next's router could write the token back after a `replaceState` carrying
    Next's own state;
  - the log exemption was broader than the two real paths (`/reports/shared?token=…`
    and `/reports/shared/<t>` were logged);
  - the reload copy blamed a valid link;
  - stale docstrings.
- **The UI review's Mediums were fixed:** the no-JS dead end on old links, a
  one-frame flash of the form on an empty fragment, the reload copy, and PDF
  button focus and announcements.

## Found, not fixed

- **The Google sign-up ticket still rides in a query string.** `routers/auth.py`
  redirects to `/sign-up/google?ticket=…`, and the web calls
  `GET /auth/google/pending?ticket=…`. Both land in Render's request log. Within
  the ticket's 10 minutes, someone reading that log could complete the sign-up
  bound to the victim's Google account. The same fragment-plus-POST treatment
  would close it.
- **Path-form share links sent before this change stay alive, and are logged when
  opened.** Re-sharing refreshes the same token's expiry, so each re-share gives
  those old copies another 30 days. Only revoke-then-share retires them.
- **CORS does not expose `Content-Disposition`,** so the web names the PDF with
  its own fallback (`<slug>-ai-visibility.pdf`, the same rule the server uses).
  The security review judged adding `expose_headers=["Content-Disposition"]`
  negligible risk.
- **`.avp-btn` has no `[aria-disabled]` styling,** so a busy PDF button only
  changes its label.
- **`apps/web` has no DOM test environment,** so the hash-change and focus
  behaviour is pinned by source and static-markup tests, not exercised.
- **The CI floors in `infra/ci/floors.json` were not raised.**

## Verified

**API 1620 → 1645 (+25).**
- `tests/test_token_links.py`: every builder puts the token after `#` and never
  before it, with or without a trailing slash on the base.
- `TestTheTokenIsNotInThePath` in `test_share_link.py`:
  - the minted URL carries the token only in the fragment;
  - the old GETs answer 404 and GETs on the new paths 405;
  - bad bodies answer 422 on both routes;
  - a 512-character token is an ordinary 404;
  - both routes send `private, no-store`, and the PDF keeps its attachment
    header and `%PDF` bytes;
  - the token is absent from structlog, caplog and stdout.
- `test_logging_config.py` adds the three bypass shapes, redacted, and the two
  exact paths, kept.
- The other suites that used the old paths or link shapes moved to the new ones.

**Web 1023 → 1052 (+29).**
- `lib/api.publicReport.test.ts` (4): POST with the token only in the body, a
  404 becomes `ApiProblem`, the filename comes from `Content-Disposition`, and
  the signed-in PDF stays a GET by scan id.
- `app/fragmentRoutes.test.tsx`:
  - the fragment parser;
  - a neutral server render;
  - invite and reset clear the fragment, share does not;
  - `replaceState(null, …)`;
  - the hashchange listener only on share;
  - the invalid state derived in render;
  - `FragmentRedirect`'s `location.replace`, anchor and `<noscript>`;
  - no web source builds `/share/${`, `/invite/${`, `/reset-password/${` or
    `/reports/${`.
- `DownloadPdfButton.test.tsx` (+4) covers `aria-disabled`, the status region
  and `aria-describedby`.
- `referrerPolicy.test.ts` covers the three fragment routes.

**Negative controls.**
- With the old lookahead put back in `logs.py`, the `?token=` and `/shared/<t>`
  cases fail (2 failed).
- With `publicReportPdf` put back to a token path, the web test fails.
- Both files were restored byte-for-byte, checked with `cmp`.

**The rest of the bar.**
- Workers 13, shared-types 53, and the full design-system suite 649.
- ruff clean; mypy 47, under its 50 ceiling.
- All typechecks clean, and all six count gates through `assert_count.py`.
- Both `uv lock --check` runs pass, and `alembic upgrade head` and
  `alembic check` pass.
- The OpenAPI contract and `api.gen.ts` were regenerated: two operations
  swapped and descriptions updated.
- `next build` passes from a copy: `/share`, `/invite` and `/reset-password`
  are static, and the three `[token]` routes are thin redirects.
- Exit codes were read from files.

# Stripe webhook events are applied once and in order

**2026-09-30, the second entry of the day.** One item, one commit.

**One migration, and no new setting.** Revision `7c1d4e9a2b53` adds the table
`stripe_webhook_events` and the nullable column `agencies.stripe_event_at`. The
container runs it before serving. It sets `lock_timeout = '5s'`, so a long
transaction on `agencies` fails the deploy instead of queueing every request.
Deploy while Stripe shows no pending webhook retries, because the watermark
starts empty. The runbook has a new "Live Stripe test (test mode on Render)"
section.

## 1. What it fixes

Before this change, a retried or out-of-order delivery could overwrite newer
billing state (for example, bring a cancelled agency back to active). Now:

- Each handled event is applied at most once, keyed on its Stripe id, in the
  same transaction as its change. Concurrent duplicates block on the primary key
  and then conflict.
- The agency row is locked `FOR UPDATE` on every lookup route (metadata
  `agency_id`, subscription id, customer id) before the ledger insert. That both
  serialises events for one agency and avoids a deadlock between the ledger's
  foreign-key lock and the unique `stripe_subscription_id` update.
- Subscription events older than the newest applied one are `stale`. Checkout
  does not move the watermark, so the subscription event carrying the period
  end still applies after it.
- A same-subscription state-machine guard: a `canceled` or `incomplete_expired`
  status is never overwritten, and `incomplete` never overwrites another status.
  This covers same-second ties and retries.
- Non-subscription checkouts are ignored.
- Unmatched events are not recorded, so a Resend after linking applies.
- An event without a numeric `created` is ignored and never sets the watermark
  from our clock.
- Log lines are `stripe.webhook.{applied,duplicate,stale,ignored,unmatched,rejected}`.
  `billing.webhook_*` is renamed and found nowhere else. The logs carry the
  event id, type and agency id, and never the payload or an email.

## 2. Reviews

- **The first security review found one High:** the metadata route was not
  locked, so concurrent updated@T2 and deleted@T3 could leave a cancelled
  agency active and move the watermark back. It also found two Mediums (the
  deadlock, and same-second ties and retries) and five Lows. All were fixed.
- **A re-review confirmed all fixed.** Its new Lows were also fixed: checkout
  moving the watermark, non-subscription checkouts, and the migration's lock
  order (it now adds the column first, taking ACCESS EXCLUSIVE once).

## Found, not fixed

- **Checkout does not refuse an agency that already has an active subscription.**
  Two tabs opened before the first payment, or a new checkout while the old plan
  runs to its end, can create a second subscription. The stored pointer then
  follows whichever subscription's event is newest, so a `deleted` for the old
  one can show the agency `canceled` while the new one is paid. Refusing checkout
  while active changes what a person sees, so it is left for a decision.
- **An operator editing a subscription's metadata in the Stripe dashboard** to
  name a different agency than the stored customer would hit
  `uq_agencies_stripe_customer_id` and answer 500 on every retry. None of our
  own flows produce that.
- **The ledger's `stale` covers both timestamp-stale and guarded events.**
- **The ledger has no retention rule.** It gains about one row per subscription
  change.
- **The CI floors in `infra/ci/floors.json` were not raised.**

## Verified

**API 1645 → 1674 (+29).**
- New tests in `tests/test_billing.py`:
  - a duplicate delivery applies once;
  - four concurrent deliveries of one id apply once;
  - a two-session proof that the conflicting insert blocks;
  - a two-session proof that the metadata route locks the agency row;
  - concurrent deleted@T3 and updated@T2 on the metadata route always end
    `canceled` with the watermark at T3 (both orderings, 6 iterations each);
  - three first-checkout events delivered together do not deadlock, end active
    and set the period end;
  - an older event arriving late is stale;
  - same-second events apply in order;
  - a retried `created` does not regress to `incomplete`;
  - `updated` or checkout after `deleted` does not resurrect;
  - a new subscription id after a cancellation applies;
  - a subscription update delivered after a newer checkout still applies and
    sets the period end;
  - non-subscription checkouts (payment mode, setup mode, a null subscription)
    are ignored and cannot undo a cancellation;
  - an unmatched event writes no row and applies when resent;
  - an event without a numeric `created` is ignored;
  - a handler failure rolls back the ledger row and the retry applies;
  - the watermark only moves forward.
  - `test_facts_only.py` now covers the ledger model.
- **Negative controls.** Each file was restored byte-for-byte afterwards and
  checked with `cmp`.
  - Removing the metadata lock fails 3 of 3 metadata-route tests on all three
    runs.
  - Forcing the guard off fails 3 tests.
  - Disabling the stale check fails the out-of-order test.
  - Letting checkout advance the watermark fails 2 tests.
- **The rest of the bar.**
  - Workers 13, shared-types 53, design-system 649, web 1052.
  - ruff clean; mypy 47, under its 50 ceiling.
  - Typechecks clean, and all six count gates through `assert_count.py`.
  - Both `uv lock --check` runs pass.
  - `alembic upgrade head`, `check`, and a downgrade/upgrade round trip pass
    on avp_dev.
  - The OpenAPI contract and `api.gen.ts` are regenerated for `WebhookAck`.
  - Exit codes were read from files.
# A scan stranded by a restart fails after 15 minutes, and a scan holds its slot exactly while it is alive

**2026-09-30, the third entry of the day.** One item, one commit.

**One migration, and no new setting.** Revision `3e8a5b7c9d14` adds the nullable column `scans.submitted_at`, under `lock_timeout = '5s'`, with no backfill.

## 1. What a person sees

- A scan started seconds before Render restarted the API (every deploy does) used
  to read "queued" for ever.
- It still holds its slot and reads queued for 15 minutes after it was started.
  After that, the next poll of the scan, the next start, or the dashboard shows
  it `failed` with `EXECUTOR_NEVER_STARTED`.
- It never counts against the allowance, and starting that client again makes a
  fresh scan.
- A scan left open by competitor detection alone is never touched, so detect now
  and scan tomorrow still works.

## 2. The mechanism

- `scans.submitted_at` is stamped when a scan is handed to the executor, inside
  the transaction that holds the allowance's `FOR UPDATE` lock, so a concurrent
  start sees it.
- `scan_executor.fail_never_started_scans` fails only QUEUED rows with
  `submitted_at` older than `IN_FLIGHT_WINDOW`. It runs inside
  `reap_stale_scans` and, scoped to one scan, in `GET /scans/{scanId}` when a
  Python check says it is due.
- The executor's claim now refuses a row that is already reapable.

## 3. The allowance, which was wrong in three ways that this closes

- An adopted detection row kept its old `created_at`, so it was not counted
  while it ran. At the free cap, two quick starts on two detected clients both
  began; now the second gets `402` `SCAN_LIMIT_FREE_USED`.
- The paid monthly period dated scans by `created_at`, so a detection row opened
  on the 30th and scanned on the 1st never counted in the new month.
- A RUNNING scan stopped holding its slot 15 minutes in, although a legitimate
  run can last up to 40 (`MAX_SCAN_DURATION`, with a live lease).
- Now a scan is dated by `coalesce(submitted_at, created_at)`. QUEUED holds a
  slot for 15 minutes from then; RUNNING holds one while its lease is live
  (unleased script runs keep the 15-minute rule).

## 4. Review

The security review found no Critical or High. Its two Mediums (the monthly date
and RUNNING by age) and one Low (a late claim of a reapable row) were fixed,
along with a no-op UPDATE on every poll.

## Found, not fixed

- **A scan that hits the 40-minute deadline ends FAILED after its engine answers
  are paid for and stored, and FAILED never counts.** `page.evaluate` in the
  technical audit has no timeout, so a site that stalls its own page could make
  this happen on purpose and read the engine results without using the free scan.
  It needs an audit timeout, and a decision on whether such a scan counts.
- **No web screen shows a failed scan's `errorCode` or `errorDetail`,** so the
  reason for a failure is not visible to a person.
- **The scan id excluded from the count comes from a read taken before the
  lock.** It is not reachable in practice (it needs a lock wait of minutes);
  re-reading after the lock would close it.
- **The CI floors in `infra/ci/floors.json` were not raised.**

## Verified

**API 1674 → 1690 (+16).**
- New tests in `test_scan_executor.py` and `test_scan_allowance.py`:
  - a submitted QUEUED scan past the window is failed by the start POST and by
    `GET /scans/{id}`, and a fresh scan then runs to `succeeded`;
  - one inside the window is neither failed nor uncounted;
  - a three-day-old detection-only row is never failed and is adopted with the
    same id;
  - a failed scan cannot be claimed late, and a reapable QUEUED row cannot be
    claimed even before the reaper runs;
  - another agency's stranded scan is a 404 and stays QUEUED;
  - `GET` on a fresh QUEUED scan does not call the reaper;
  - the adoption race: 202 then 402 at the free cap;
  - a stranded submission frees its slot;
  - a last-month detection row scanned this month counts this month;
  - a RUNNING scan with a live lease 20 minutes in holds the slot and one with
    an expired lease does not;
  - an unleased RUNNING row counts at 1 minute and not at 16.

**Negative controls,** each file restored byte-for-byte and checked with `cmp`:
  - an age-only reap rule fails the detection-only test;
  - counting by `created_at` fails the adoption test;
  - dating the month by `created_at` fails the month test;
  - an age-only RUNNING rule fails the live-lease test;
  - dropping the claim guard fails the late-claim test.

**The rest of the bar.**
  - Workers 13, shared-types 53, design-system 649, web 1052.
  - ruff clean; mypy 47, under its 50 ceiling.
  - Typechecks clean, and all six count gates through `assert_count.py`.
  - Both `uv lock --check` runs pass.
  - `alembic upgrade head` and `check` pass, with a downgrade/upgrade round trip
    on avp_dev.
  - The OpenAPI contract regenerates byte-identically.
  - Exit codes were read from files.
# Login, sign-up and reset requests are rate-limited per email and per IP

**2026-09-30, the fourth entry of the day.** One item, one commit.

**No migration. New optional settings, all with defaults:** `LOGIN_LIMIT_PER_EMAIL`, `LOGIN_LIMIT_PER_IP`, `LOGIN_WINDOW_SECONDS`, `SIGNUP_LIMIT_PER_EMAIL`, `SIGNUP_LIMIT_PER_IP`, `SIGNUP_WINDOW_SECONDS`, `RESET_LIMIT_PER_EMAIL`, `RESET_LIMIT_PER_IP`, `RESET_WINDOW_SECONDS`, and `CLIENT_IP_HEADER` (empty). **Run the runbook's new client-IP probe after deploy.**

## 1. What a person sees

After too many attempts, the sign-in, sign-up and forgot-password forms show
"Too many attempts. Try again in N minutes." Successful sign-ins do not count.
A reset, once completed, clears the count for that address. With Redis down,
sign-in and sign-up say the service is unavailable (they could not create a
session anyway), and forgot-password still gives its usual reply.

## 2. The mechanism

- `services/rate_limit.py`: fixed-window counters in Redis, one Lua script per
  request. The IP bucket is checked first, and a request refused by IP writes
  no email key.
- Keys are `rl:{action}:{kind}:` plus a 16-byte HMAC of the normalised email or
  IP, keyed from `APP_SECRET`, so neither is stored in the clear. Every check
  runs before argon2 or any database work.
- Client IP is uvicorn's address by default, or the header named by
  `CLIENT_IP_HEADER`. It is parsed with `ipaddress`: IPv4 is keyed exactly,
  IPv6 per /64, and v4-mapped addresses as IPv4. An unparseable value, or a
  configured header that is missing, shares one bucket and is logged without
  its value.
- The 429 is the existing `RateLimited` problem, now with `Retry-After`. The
  new 503 `service-unavailable` covers login and sign-up when Redis errors.
- Log lines are `auth.rate_limited` (action and kind only),
  `auth.rate_limit.unavailable`, `auth.rate_limit.ip_unparsed` and
  `auth.rate_limit.ip_header_missing`.
- Web: the three forms show the server's detail for a 429; forgot-password no
  longer calls it a connection error.

## 3. Review

- **The first security review raised one High, not confirmed:** on Render the
  per-IP bucket may key on a client-chosen `X-Forwarded-For`. It is hardened
  in code, and the runbook probe settles which header to trust.
- **It also raised three Mediums** (IPv6 /128 buckets; refused requests writing
  new email keys that could fill Key Value; a victim locked out by counted
  attempts, with successes counted too) and two Lows (fail-open gaining nothing
  on login and sign-up; unvalidated settings). All were fixed.
- **This change also briefly took mypy from 47 to 48;** that was fixed without
  an ignore.

## Found, not fixed

- **A person can still be kept out of password sign-in** by someone who sends
  11 wrong passwords for their address every 15 minutes. A completed reset
  clears the count until the next round. Existing sessions and Google sign-in
  (which links a verified Google address) are unaffected. The full fix is a
  per-device budget (a signed "known device" cookie), a design decision left
  open.
- **The per-email count shows recent activity on an address:** a limit tripping
  early, and its `Retry-After`, show that someone else tried that address
  recently. This comes with any per-subject counter.
- **`CLIENT_IP_HEADER` is empty until the runbook probe is run on Render.**
- **A re-review after the fixes** found no new defect in the code. Left open:
  a limit keyed per (email, IP) with a looser per-email ceiling would stop
  the lock-out above, and is a design decision; IPv6 is keyed per /64, so a
  tunnelled /48 still yields many buckets; `POST /auth/change-password` has no
  limit (older than this change); and the Redis pool has no
  `socket_timeout`, so a Redis that hangs rather than refusing makes sign-in
  hang instead of answering 503.
- **The CI floors in `infra/ci/floors.json` were not raised.**

## Verified

**API 1690 → 1749 (+59).** `tests/test_auth_rate_limit.py`, 59 tests, covering:
- the defaults;
- for each route, the (N+1)th attempt answering 429 with `Retry-After`, per
  email and per IP;
- the window resetting;
- reset 200s and 429s byte-identical for known and unknown addresses;
- sign-up tripping before the 409;
- IP parsing (garbage, ports, scopes, a missing configured header never
  falling back to `X-Forwarded-For`), IPv6 /64 grouping and v4-mapped
  addresses;
- no new email keys once the IP bucket trips;
- successful logins giving their attempt back, with the counter floored at 0;
- a reset-confirm clearing the login count;
- Redis down: 503 for login and sign-up, the usual 200 for reset;
- settings of 0 or −1 rejected;
- no email or IP in any key or log line.

**Web 1052 → 1056 (+4):** the 429 branch of each of the three forms.

**Negative controls,** each file restored byte-for-byte and checked with `cmp`:
- bypassing the login check fails its tests;
- removing the give-back on success fails 3 tests;
- putting the email count before the IP check fails 3 tests.

**The rest of the bar.**
- Workers 13, shared-types 53, design-system 649.

# A stock Tailwind class anywhere in apps/web or packages fails the design-system suite

**2026-09-30, the eighth entry of the day.** One item, one commit.

**Render: nothing to set.**

## 1. What changed

- **`packages/design-system/src/tailwind-preset.ts` replaces colours, spacing, fontFamily, fontSize, borderRadius and boxShadow,** so a stock class such as `bg-white text-gray-500 text-sm shadow-md` compiles to nothing. The existing guards in `packages/design-system/src/tokens/reportIsolation.test.ts` (~218-340) only caught numeric spacing suffixes, `-semantic-` colours and bad line/surface/text/on or rounded-* suffixes.
- **The test file found 0 stock classes in the tree.** Before this change, the bar would have missed them during build and all suites.

## 2. The mechanism

- New `packages/design-system/src/tokens/stockClasses.ts`: a scanner that imports the preset object and reads spacing, fontSize, boxShadow, borderRadius, fontFamily and colours (nested keys and shades) from it, so a future token is allowed automatically. The only hard-coded vocabulary is Tailwind's own stock names (the palette names, white/black/transparent/current/inherit, stock text sizes, shadows, families); each is a finding unless the preset defines the same key. It flags stock colours on bg, text, border-*, ring, ring-offset, outline, fill, stroke, from/via/to, divide, placeholder, decoration, accent, caret and shadow; stock text sizes and shadows; any rounded[-side][-key] whose key is not in the preset; font-sans/font-serif; numeric spacing outside the preset scale on p/m/gap/space, w/h/min/max, inset/top/right/bottom/left, translate and basis. Arbitrary `[...]` values are skipped.
- A small character-level tokenizer: strips //, /* */ and JSX {/* */} comments; scans ', " and template literals (with ${} bodies scanned as code); keeps line numbers; CSS is scanned only in @apply bodies. A bare word (`shadow`, `rounded`) counts as a class only when at least half the tokens in that string look like utilities, which keeps prose out.
- New `packages/design-system/src/tokens/stockClasses.test.ts`: fixture tests (each category flagged; real preset classes and prefix-sharing utilities not flagged) plus a tree test over `apps/web/src` and every `packages/*/src` (ts, tsx, css; skips node_modules, dist, .next, dist-styleguide, tests) asserting zero findings and printing file:line:class for any.
- One scanner false positive was found and fixed (the word `shadow` in a prose `note=` string in `packages/design-system/src/styleguide/Styleguide.tsx:381`). The two comments that mention `bg-slate-500` (tailwind-preset.ts header, ReportView.tsx:14) are not flagged.

## Found, not fixed

- **Known limits:** a class glued to an interpolation (`p-${x}`) is not checked; prose with many hyphenated words could in theory false-positive.

## Verified

**Design-system vitest 649 → 839 (+190).**
- Red first: the 190 new tests ran against a stub scanner and 60 failed (the fixture tests: each category flagged; real preset classes and prefix-sharing utilities not flagged). With the scanner implemented, all 190 pass.
- `infra/ci/floors.json`: `design-system-vitest` 606 → 839 (it was already 43 behind at 649).
- Tree test asserting zero findings across all source files.
- Negative control: `bg-white text-sm shadow-md` added to `apps/web/src/components/report/ReportView.tsx:186` → the design-system suite exited 1 (1 failed, 838 passed) naming all three at ReportView.tsx:186; the file was restored byte-for-byte with `cp` and verified with `cmp`.

**The rest of the bar.**
- API pytest 1751, workers 13, shared-types 53, web 1068, mypy 47 (ceiling 50).
- ruff clean; all typechecks clean; all six count gates through `assert_count.py` pass.
- Both `uv lock --check` runs pass; no schema change, so Alembic was not run.
