# The PDF report is typeset: cells wrap instead of being cut, a continued table repeats its header, nothing is stranded at a page foot, and the pitch beat says what the second number would take

**2026-10-07 (built, barred and controlled that evening; committed 2026-10-08), the third entry of the day; branch `pilot-fixes-7`, item 3 of the founder's brief of 2026-10-07 (the RMIT University report).** The PDF writer, the PDF document and the web report, with one bar.

**Render: nothing to set.** The change is in how a report is drawn and worded. No stored report is rewritten; the next one a client opens or downloads reads as below.

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 5, Presentation (the report a client reads, on screen and as a PDF); lifecycle phase: Activation (Epic 9), the artefact the pilot agency actually hands over.

## 1. What was wrong

Five cosmetic defects, all seen in the RMIT University report of 2026-10-05:

- **Table cells were cut, not wrapped.** `_truncate` cut any cell that did not fit on one line, so the rival column printed "Swinburne University of Tec…". A client's own competitor set is the one thing in the report they can check by eye, and the names were unreadable.
- **A table that ran onto a new page lost its header.** Page 3 opened with a bare row, `desk365.io  1  —`, under no columns.
- **Labels and headings could end a page.** "03 THE EVIDENCE" sat alone at the foot of page 1, its heading overleaf.
- **A paragraph could leave one line behind.** The widow and orphan cases were not handled at all; the colophon's rule and text were in the flow, so the footer could take a page of its own.
- **The pitch beat's second number was unexplained.** It read "58 today. 99 with the fixes above." — a number with no stated basis, and the only arithmetic a reader could do (99 − 58) was not printed. The cover and the web letterhead also printed the agency's URL slug beside its name, and the web report ended on a "Beats score · gap · proof · fix · pitch" line, which names this system's internals rather than anything the scan found.

## 2. What changed

**The writer (`pdf.py`).**

- **Cells wrap.** `cell_lines()` wraps a cell to at most two lines and cuts the second with an ellipsis; `row_height()` makes a row as tall as its tallest cell, plus `MULTILINE_PAD` when any cell wrapped. A row never splits across a page: one that does not fit moves whole. `_truncate` is gone.
- **A continued table repeats its header.** `draw_header()` draws the header, its rule and its spacing; `table()` calls it again on every page the rows continue onto, so a header is never two lines on one page and one on the next.
- **Nothing is stranded.** `_keep_with_next(own, follow)` is the single check behind the eyebrow, heading and subheading calls: it starts a new page unless the element plus the first `follow` points of what comes next fit. `keep_together(height)` holds a beat's rule, label and heading's first line together.
- **One widow and orphan rule.** `_plan_paragraph(count, leading)` is used by both `text()` and `bullet()`: a paragraph of three lines or fewer never splits; a longer one never leaves fewer than two lines on either side of a break.
- **The footer is drawn in the bottom margin of the last page**, at `FOOTER_Y`, with its own hairline, outside the flow — so it costs no flow space and can never start a page of its own. `footer(text)` stores it; `render()` appends its operators to the last page only.
- **The no-break space is a character this writer can draw.** U+00A0 joins `_WINANSI_EXTRA` as WinAnsi 0o240 at the space's own width, its transliteration to a plain space is dropped, and `wrap()` splits on the plain space only, so a no-break space is carried into the word it joins.

**The document (`report_pdf.py`) and the web report (`ReportView.tsx`).**

- **The pitch heading** is now "{t} today. Up to {a} if these fixes close every gap they address ({t} + {d})." — `t` and `a` are the two **printed** (rounded) figures and `d` is the difference **of those two printed figures**, never a separately rounded one, so the sum always equals the number beside it (58.24 and 98.84 print "58 today. Up to 99 … (58 + 41).", not "58 + 40"). When the two printed numbers are equal there is nothing to add and it prints only "{t} today." The parenthetical is joined by no-break spaces, on the PDF and on the web, so it is never split across two lines. `_pitch_heading` and `pitchHeading` produce the same sentence character for character and each names the other.
- **The row label** "Composite if they all land" is now "Composite if every gap they address closes", which says what the figure is conditional on.
- **The agency slug is gone** from the PDF cover and the web letterhead (the agency's name stays), and the web report's "Beats …" line is gone. Neither was anything the scan measured.

## Found, not fixed

- **The last page can hold very little.** In the RMIT report the closing three-line paragraph does not fit under the figure rows on page 3 — it would cross the bottom margin — so the widow rule moves it whole and page 4 carries it and the footer alone. That is the rule working; a page that is mostly white is the cost of never stranding a line.
- **The heading and the paragraph under it are gated differently** (the UI review's only should-fix, and the same split on the PDF). The heading now asks whether the two **printed** figures differ; the web's `canProject` and the PDF's figure rows still ask whether the **raw** recoverable points are above zero. They disagree in one case: raw points above zero but too small to move the rounded composite (composite 62.6, potential 62.9, recoverable 0.3 — a pair the suite already pins). The heading then reads "63 today." while the paragraph below reads "scores 63 today … recovers 0.3 points, which is a composite of 63": both sentences are true, and the paragraph says outright that the figure is the same weighted sum, but it prints the same rounded number either side of a gain, which is the confusion the heading change was made to remove. **Not changed here, because the fix needs copy the founder has not seen:** simply moving `canProject` onto the printed figures would fall through to "There is no projection to make from this scan … this scan does not have one yet", which is false for a scan that has a score. It is checklist row 3.99.
- **A cell longer than two lines is still cut** with an ellipsis. Two lines is the cap that keeps a table scannable; the web report does not truncate these names at all.
- **The web beat heading's measure is capped at 22 characters** (`.avp-beat__heading`, unchanged here). Every beat heading already wraps against it; this one is now the longest in the report (73 characters against 43 to 64 for the others), so it wraps about one line further than its siblings. Worth the founder's eye on a rendered report.
- **The footnote under the fix list is tight** against the list above it.

## Verified

**API pytest 5616 → 5656 (+40); web vitest 2570 → 2581 (+11). Both floors are raised to match.**

- **New:** `test_report_pdf.py` 66 → 106 tests covering, each against the drawn page rather than the source: wrapped cells and their alignment, the two-line cap and its ellipsis, row height and the multi-line pad, a row moving whole, the repeated header on a continuation page, keep-with-next for the eyebrow, heading and subheading, the beat's rule-label-heading group, the widow and orphan rule and its split point, the footer drawn once in the last page's bottom margin, the pitch sentence for six composite/potential pairs including the two equal cases, the no-break space surviving `normalise` and emitted as WinAnsi 0o240, the sum held whole at five measures, a plain space still breaking a line, and the renamed row label. The web suite pins the same six pairs, the no-break spaces in the rendered report, and the absence of the slug and the "Beats …" line.
- **The test's text extractor no longer collapses the no-break space.** It joined and collapsed with `\s+`, which flattens U+00A0 — an assertion could then pass against a sentence the writer never produced. It now collapses every whitespace character but that one.
- **On this tree,** each file restored and its bytes checked after:
  - the sum joined by plain spaces again: 6 of the 106 tests in `test_report_pdf.py` fail.
  - `wrap()` breaking on every space again: 2.
  - the no-break space off the WinAnsi table (so it is dropped rather than drawn): 3.
  - the renamed row label reverted: 1.
  - the widow and orphan rule off: 3.
  - keep-with-next off: 2.
  - the web sum joined by plain spaces again: 8 of the 445 report-component tests fail.
- **The rest of the bar** (this tree, one run, 19:13 to 19:20):
  - Counts: API 5656, workers 27, shared-types 53 (0 fail), design-system 967, web 2581, mypy 42 (ceiling 50).
  - All six count gates pass through `assert_count.py`.
  - Ruff is clean, all typechecks pass, and the styleguide builds.
  - Both `uv lock --check` runs pass, and Alembic upgrade and check pass on an empty database.
  - The Python licence audits pass in both environments, and the JavaScript audit passes (`pnpm licenses list --json`).
  - OpenAPI and `api.gen.ts` regenerate with no change.
- **Every page was looked at.** The RMIT/Swinburne fixture renders to four pages: the cover with beats 01 and 02; "03 THE EVIDENCE" opening page 2 with its tables; page 3 repeating the sources header, then beat 04 and the pitch heading and figure rows; page 4 the closing paragraph and the footer. No stranded heading, no lone body line, no cut rival name, and the sum whole on one line.
- Exit codes were read from files.

# When the points a fix recovers do not move the printed score, the report says so rather than printing the same number twice

**2026-10-08; branch `pilot-fixes-7`, checklist 3.99, the founder's decision of 2026-10-08.** The PDF document and the web report, with its own bar.

**Render: nothing to set.** Wording and a gate; no stored report is rewritten.

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 5, Presentation (the report a client reads, on screen and as a PDF); lifecycle phase: Activation (Epic 9).

## 1. What was wrong

The pitch heading and the paragraph under it asked different questions, found by the UI review of item 3 (`7f63842`).

- **The heading** asks whether the two **printed** figures differ: when they do not, it prints only "100 today." and claims no uplift.
- **The paragraph under it, and the PDF's figure rows,** still asked whether the **raw** recoverable points were above zero.

They disagree whenever points worth recovering do not move the rounded score. The reachable case is the cap: a composite of 99.6 already prints as 100, and `potentialComposite` is `min(100, …)`, so 2.0 points recovered still print as 100. The heading then read "100 today." while the paragraph under it read "scores 100 today … recovers 2.0 points, which is a composite of 100" — the same number either side of a gain, which is the confusion the heading change in `7f63842` was made to remove.

Moving the gate alone would have been wrong: the paragraph's other branch says "There is no projection to make from this scan … this scan does not have one yet", which is false for a scan that has a score.

## 2. What changed

- **One source for the two printed figures.** `_printed_figures(story)` in `report_pdf.py` and `printedFigures(narrative)` in `ReportView.tsx` return the two rounded numbers and their difference, or nothing when there is no score. The heading and the paragraph both read it, so they can no longer disagree about whether there is an uplift to state.
- **A third branch, for points that do not move the printed score.** The report says: "Closing the gaps listed above recovers 2.0 points, which does not change the rounded score of 100." The same sentence on the web and on the PDF, by the founder's decision of 2026-10-08.
- **The figures are still printed.** The PDF keeps its three rows: the exact composites do differ (99.60 and 100.00), and it is only the rounded pair that does not. The sentence sits above the existing arithmetic note, so what the rows mean is still stated.
- **The no-score branch is untouched** and still reached only when there is no score or nothing to recover.

## Found, not fixed

- **The cap is the only case that reaches this in practice.** Below 100 a dimension fix needs a gap of at least 2 points (`MIN_GAP_POINTS`), and 2 points always move the rounded score; so the branch is exercised by a near-perfect score whose uplift is capped at 100. It is written for the general case rather than the cap.

# The pitch's three figures re-add exactly as printed: the ceiling is the composite plus the points the fixes list, not a second rounding of them

**2026-10-08; branch `pilot-fixes-8`, item A1 of the founder's brief of 2026-10-08 (RMIT University's re-run, `scan_01M4CCKWT0AB2K17CAWPVP0P83`).** The report narrative (Python and TypeScript), the web report, and the tests of the PDF and the CSV. Not a formula change: no `FORMULA_VERSION` bump, and no stored score moves.

**Render: nothing to set.**

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 1, Delivery (report rendering); lifecycle phase: Activation (Epic 9).

## 1. What was wrong

RMIT University's PDF printed, under "05 The opportunity":

| Row | Printed |
|---|---|
| Composite today | 72.48 |
| Points the listed changes recover | 25.9 |
| Composite if every gap they address closes | **98.40** |

A reader adds 72.48 + 25.9 and gets **98.38**.

**Where 98.40 came from.** Each fix's points are its gap rounded to 1dp (17.3925 → 17.4, 5.163 → 5.2, 3.333 → 3.3), and the middle row is their sum, 25.9. The ceiling was then rounded **a second time, to 1dp**: `round1(72.48 + 25.9)` = `round1(98.38)` = 98.4, which the PDF prints at 2dp as "98.40" (`report_narrative.derive_narrative` and `derive.deriveNarrative`). The same second rounding is in every report: Help Scout's test fixture printed 58.24 + 40.6 as 98.80, not 98.84, and so did item 3's rendered pages on 2026-10-07.

On the web the paragraph could not re-add either: "scores 72 today … recovers 25.9 points, which is a composite of 98", and 72 + 25.9 is 97.9.

## 2. What changed

**One rule: every total is the sum of the figures printed above it.**

- **The ceiling** is the printed composite plus the printed points, rounded to 2dp only to clear float noise (a 2dp figure plus a 1dp figure is exact at 2dp), and still capped at 100. RMIT University now reads **72.48 + 25.9 = 98.38**. The same in `derive_narrative` and `deriveNarrative`.
- **The fix list is unchanged**: each fix still prints its own points at 1dp, and the middle row and "6 changes, worth 25.9 points" are their sum, so 17.4 + 5.2 + 3.3 = 25.9 holds as before.
- **The web paragraph** now states the PDF rows' three figures: "scores 72.48 today. Closing the gaps listed above recovers 25.9 points, which is a composite of 98.38." Its last sentence said the ceiling "is what the score becomes if those dimensions reach 100"; at two places that is no longer exact (the ceiling adds the fixes' *rounded* points), so it now carries the PDF's own note, already approved: "That is arithmetic over the figures already in this report — the points the listed fixes recover, added to the score as it stands. It is not a forecast." The pitch heading keeps its whole numbers ("72 today. Up to 98 … (72 + 26)."), from the one shared `printedFigures` / `_printed_figures` helper, whose docstrings now say it gates the paragraph rather than supplying its figures.
- **The CSV** carries no total and no ceiling — only the overall score and each fix's points — so there, "re-adds" means its fixes' points sum to the report's middle row over the report's own composite. It already did; a test now holds it.
- `packages/shared-types/fixtures/expected-narrative.json` was regenerated from the TypeScript side with its own command (`AVP_WRITE_FIXTURES=1`); only `potentialComposite` moved, in each case to the exact sum (98.8 → 98.84, 88.9 → 88.94, 84.8 → 84.84).

**Why not the brief's proposal** (the middle row at 2dp, 25.89, and the exact ceiling, 98.37) — **a trade, put to the founder (checklist 3.100).** With each fix rounded to 1dp, one place on the page must show the rounding:
- **The brief's rule** makes the ceiling the exact weighted sum, and the rows re-add. But the fix list printed just above them does not: 17.4 + 5.2 + 3.3 make 25.9, under a heading and a row saying 25.89. Printing each fix at 2dp does not cure it, since 17.39 + 5.16 + 3.33 = 25.88.
- **The rule built here** makes every printed figure re-add, at every level. The ceiling is then the sum of rounded figures rather than the exact weighted sum: RMIT 98.38 against 98.3685; Help Scout's fixture 98.84 against 98.75 (its three fixes round up by 0.09 together).

The second shows its rounding only against a figure the page never prints; the first shows it between two figures printed side by side. So this rule is built, and the founder chooses.

## Found, not fixed

- **The cap (checklist 3.100, the founder's wording).** When the listed fixes cover every gap that is left — two dimensions at 100, or only three counted — their 1dp points can add up to more than 100 minus the composite, and the ceiling is held at 100: 70.53 + 29.6 prints as 100.00. The 100 is true; the rounded points overshoot. It is the one case the rows do not re-add, it was so before this change too, and it is now named in the code and pinned by a test in each language so that any change to it is deliberate.
- **The UI review (no blocker).** Taken: the sentence above, and the stale docstrings. Left for the founder with 3.100: a cue that the paragraph's 72.48 is the heading's 72 to two places. Pre-existing, not from this change: the gap beat prints a gap with `toFixed(1)` while the fix list rounds it half-up first, so on an exact half (28.95) one reads 28.9 and the other 29.0 — about 0.6% of gaps in the reviewer's sweep.
- **Correction to `pilot-fixes-7`'s 3.99 entry.** It said the equal-score branch ("…which does not change the rounded score of 100") is reached "through the cap". It cannot be reached by any self-consistent report: the gaps sum to exactly 100 − composite, and a fix needs a gap of at least 2 points, so points that exist always move the rounded score by at least one, and above a composite of 99 there are no fixes at all. The branch was only ever reached by a test whose composite did not match its sub-scores. It stays as a guard; nothing a client sees changes.

## Verified

The arithmetic under test is the same either way: the PDF's three rows read 72.48, 25.9 and 98.38 and re-add; "6 changes, worth 25.9 points"; the fixes print 17.4, 5.2 and 3.3 and sum to the middle row; and the heading reads "72 today. Up to 98 … (72 + 26)." (`test_report_pdf.py`). The CSV's fix points sum to 25.9 over its overall score of 72.48 (`test_report_csv.py`). The web paragraph and fix heading say the same (`ReportView.test.tsx`). `derive.test.ts`'s ceiling test pinned the 1dp rounding; it now pins the exact sum, and as `toBe(98.84)` rather than `toBeCloseTo(98.8, 1)`. The cap is pinned on a self-consistent payload in both languages (`test_report_narrative.py`, `derive.test.ts`): composite 70.53, ceiling 100, points overshooting.

- **Every action the workflows use ran on Node 20**, which GitHub is deprecating for actions: `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-node@v4`, `astral-sh/setup-uv@v5`, `pnpm/action-setup@v4`, `docker/setup-buildx-action@v3`, `docker/build-push-action@v6` (each tag's own `action.yml` says `using: node20`).

## 2. What changed

- **Each action moves to its first major that runs on Node 24**, read from that tag's own `action.yml` (`using: node24`) and its release notes, not guessed:

| Action | Was | Now | Its release notes, for us |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actions/checkout` | v4 | **v5** | Node 24; needs runner 2.327.1 or later (GitHub-hosted runners have it). |
| `actions/setup-node` | v4 | **v5** | Node 24; caches automatically when `package.json` names a `packageManager`. Ours already sets `cache: pnpm`, so nothing changes. |

| `docker/setup-buildx-action` | v3 | **v4** | Node 24; drops deprecated inputs and outputs, none of which we use. |
| `docker/build-push-action` | v6 | **v7** | Node 24; drops `DOCKER_BUILD_NO_SUMMARY`, `DOCKER_BUILD_EXPORT_RETENTION_DAYS` and the legacy export-build tool. We set none of them; our inputs (`context`, `file`, `load`, `tags`, `cache-from`, `cache-to`) are all kept. |

- **Unchanged on purpose:** `node-version: "22"` in the web job. That is the Node the build runs on, not the actions' runtime, and the comment beside it says why it is 22 (Node 24 breaks esbuild's service process in this workspace).

# Every line the fix generator writes names its scan, and `fixes.generated accepted=5` beside six listed fixes is as designed

**2026-10-08; branch `pilot-fixes-8`, items A4 and A5 of the founder's brief of 2026-10-08.** `services/fix_generator.py` and `services/fix_runner.py`; A5 is a finding with no code change.

**Render: nothing to set.**

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 1, Delivery (operating the pipeline: what its log lines say); lifecycle phase: Activation (Epic 9).

## 1. What was wrong

- **A4.** RMIT University's re-run logged `fixes.generated accepted=5 rejected=0 domain=rmit.edu.au …` with no `scan_id`, though every other line of a scan carries one. The cause was wider than that line: `generate_fixes` is never given the scan, so **none of the fifteen lines it and `accept()` write** carried a `scan_id` — the four rejections (`fixes.claim_rejected`, `fixes.code_rejected`, `fixes.proportion_rejected`, `fixes.domain_rejected`), the seven provider outcomes (`fixes.auth_failed`, `fixes.rate_limited`, `fixes.quota_exhausted`, `fixes.bad_request`, `fixes.timeout`, `fixes.connection_error`, `fixes.api_error`), `fixes.schema_violation`, `fixes.refused`, `fixes.reasoning` and `fixes.generated`. A refused fix in the log could not be traced to the scan it belonged to.
- **A5.** The same line said `accepted=5`, and the report showed six fixes.

## 2. What changed, and what was found

- **A4.** `generate_fixes` takes a required `scan_id` (so no caller can leave it out) and binds it once (`log = logger.bind(scan_id=scan_id)`), and every one of the fifteen lines goes through that logger. `accept()` takes it as an optional keyword, because the tests call it directly. The runner passes `scan.id`. There is no `structlog.contextvars` binding anywhere in the API, and every other scan line passes `scan_id` explicitly (`fixes.not_generated` in `fix_runner.py` among them), so this follows that pattern rather than introducing a new one.
- **A5 — no change; expected.** The report's list is up to five measured fixes (dimension gaps and audit findings) **plus one citation fix in a slot of its own on top** (`report_narrative.py`, `MAX_CITATION_FIXES = 1`, "ON TOP of MAX_FIXES"). The generator is only ever given the measured candidates (`fix_generator.build_candidates`), so it never sees the citation fix. RMIT University's six are three gap fixes (Share of Voice, Sentiment, Technical Foundation; Mention Rate's and Citation Strength's gaps are under the 2-point floor), two audit fixes (FAQPage schema is one) — the five the generator worded — and **"Get onto unsw.edu.au", the deterministic citation fix**, whose domain comes from the scan's cited domains and is never written by the model.

And in `test_fix_runner.py`, `TestTheRunnerNamesTheScan` runs the runner itself (`generate_for_scan`) on a real scan with the provider unreachable: the generator's `fixes.connection_error` and the runner's `fixes.not_generated` both carry **that scan's** id, which is what production's lines depend on. The six existing `generate_fixes` calls pass a `scan_id`.

The targeted run had covered only the fix generator's own files. Both now pass a `scan_id`; `scripts/verify_e2e.py` wraps the function with `*args, **kwargs` and needed nothing. The bar below is the re-run.

# An explicit re-score of a scan matched before v7 is refused, and every scan now records which matching rule made its matches

**2026-10-08; branch `pilot-fixes-8`, item A6 of the founder's brief of 2026-10-08 (launch checklist 3.97, decided 2026-10-08).** The scan model, one migration, the scan runner, the re-score route, and the contracts.

**Render: nothing to set.** Migration `5863629b56ab` runs before the API serves (launch checklist 1.1j); deploy while no scan is in flight.

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 2, Measurement (the provenance of what a scan stored); lifecycle phase: Retention (Epic 11), whose before/after reporting depends on a score meaning what its version says.

## 1. What was wrong

`FORMULA_VERSION` v7 (2026-10-07) changed **how a brand is matched** (`extraction.find_brand`: a 2-4 character short form in capitals), not only the arithmetic. Answer text is never stored, so a scan matched before v7 can never be matched again. `POST /scans/{scanId}/score` re-scores from the stored matches and wrote a row labelled `v7` from matches v7 never made, and nothing on the report said so. Nothing recorded which rule matched a scan: `Scan.formula_version` is never written anywhere in `src` (every row holds its `v1` default), and `BrandMention` has no version column.

## 2. What changed

- **`extraction.MATCHER_VERSION = "v7"`**: the rule `find_brand` applies, named by the formula version at which it arrived. It moves **only** when what matching finds changes, never on a weights or formula-only change, which leaves stored matches as good as they were; a test pins it beside `FORMULA_VERSION` and says the two move separately.
- **`scans.matcher_version`** (NOT NULL), stamped by `scan_runner.run_scan` at the RUNNING transition beside `engine_versions`: the process that runs a scan is the one that matches it, so a scan an older instance queued and this one runs is stamped by this one. Its two defaults differ on purpose. In Python it is the current matcher, since every scan the ORM creates is matched by this code. In the database it is `'pre-v7'`, meaning "not recorded": that is what a row written without the column reads, and refusing a re-score of such a row is the safe direction.
- **Migration `5863629b56ab`** adds the column under `lock_timeout = '5s'` and runs one statement, `BACKFILL_V7_MATCHED`. A scan is `'v7'` when it has at least one score and every score it has is `v7`, meaning its own run scored it under v7; every other scan stays `'pre-v7'`.
  - **Why not "every existing row is pre-v7":** production can hold scans run after v7 deployed (the founder's brief describes RMIT University's re-run, made after it), and marking those pre-v7 would refuse a re-score that is fine.
  - **A pre-v7 scan explicitly re-scored after the deploy** keeps its older row (v5), so it correctly stays pre-v7.
  - The statement only touches rows still `'pre-v7'`, so it can be run again safely.
- **The refusal.** After the agency check and the failed-scan check, on the row read under the same `FOR UPDATE` lock, a scan whose `matcher_version` is not the current matcher's gets `409 /problems/conflict` with "This scan's brand matches were made under an earlier rule, and answer text is not kept, so it cannot be re-scored under the current one. Run a new scan instead." No Score row is written or refreshed. Another agency's scan is still the same `404` as an unknown one, and a failed scan keeps its own `409`. A scan's own run still scores it at the end.
- **Contracts:** `docs/api-contracts.md` and the route's docstring list the new 409; `openapi.json` (one description) and `api.gen.ts` (its JSDoc) are regenerated. `docs/scoring-spec.md`'s v7 row no longer says such a re-score "uses its stored matches".

## Found, not fixed

- **One generic 409.** The refusal uses `/problems/conflict`, as 3.30's failed-scan refusal does, so a client tells the two apart by `detail`. No web code calls this route. A dedicated problem type is a small subclass if it is ever wanted.
- **The pin guards the constant, not the behaviour.** Nothing ties `find_brand`'s results to `MATCHER_VERSION`, so a change to matching without a bump would go unnoticed; a golden-case fingerprint test would close it.
- **The backfill runs in the same revision as the column**, holding the table's lock for the update. Measured on a scratch database: 20,004 scans and 20,004 scores upgraded in 0.63 s. Production's count was not measured, and is far smaller.

# The API's access log keeps the method, the path and the status, and no longer the visitor's IP address

**2026-10-08; branch `pilot-fixes-8`, item A3 of the founder's brief of 2026-10-08.** `apps/api/src/avp_api/logs.py`, two flags on the `exec uvicorn` line of `apps/api/docker-entrypoint.sh`, and their tests. Rate limiting, `CLIENT_IP_HEADER` and the entrypoint's `--proxy-headers` flags are untouched.

**Render: nothing to set.** The next deploy's access lines read ` - "GET /api/v1/dashboard HTTP/1.1" 200 OK`.

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 0, Trust substrate (what the product keeps about the people who use it); lifecycle phase: Activation (Epic 9), before pilots' visitors reach the API.

## 1. What was wrong

Every API access line began with the visitor's address: `INFO: 120.21.136.90:0 - "GET /api/v1/dashboard HTTP/1.1" 200 OK`. uvicorn runs with `--proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*'` (`apps/api/docker-entrypoint.sh`), so that is the visitor's own IP, from the proxy's `X-Forwarded-For`, and Render keeps stdout. Nothing reads it from the log: rate limiting reads the address from the request itself (`services/rate_limit.py`, `CLIENT_IP_HEADER`).

## 2. What changed

- **`DropClientAddress`** (`logs.py`), a filter on uvicorn's access logger beside the existing `RedactSecretPaths`, blanks the address before the line is formatted. uvicorn's own access formatter unpacks exactly five arguments (client, method, path, HTTP version, status), so the address is replaced with `""` rather than removed: the line then reads as uvicorn's own line does for a request that has no client. A record of any other shape passes through untouched.
- **Installed where `RedactSecretPaths` is,** in `configure_logging`, which `create_app` calls, so it applies to whatever command imports the app; uvicorn configures its loggers before importing it, so the filter is not overwritten. Idempotent.
- **Two more ways uvicorn could print the address are closed on the entrypoint's line** (found by the security review):
  - **`--ws none`.** uvicorn logs a WebSocket handshake on its *error* logger, address first, where the access filter never looks, and with the path unredacted. The API has no websocket route (a test already pins that), so no product page opens one, but a scanner can: on the real server, with the flag removed, a handshake logged `INFO: 203.0.113.9:0 - "WebSocket /api/v1/reports/Tk-abc_123XYZ" 403`, which is the visitor's address and a token. With `--ws none`, an upgrade is served as plain HTTP, through the filtered access line.
  - **`--log-level info`.** uvicorn reads `UVICORN_*` variables, so `UVICORN_LOG_LEVEL=debug` or `trace` on Render would print request headers and whole scopes, address and token paths included. A flag on the line beats the variable.
- The method, the path (still redacted of secrets, as before) and the status are kept, as the brief asks. The module's docstring says why the address went, and the entrypoint says why each flag is there.

## Found, not fixed

- **No other API log line carries an IP address** (every `logger.*` call checked for an `ip`, `client_ip`, `client_host` or `remote_addr` field).
- **`/privacy` was not edited,** as the brief says. A note for the lawyer under 2.4: `PrivacyPolicy.tsx:204` ("The API's server log records each request: the IP address it came from…") now says more is kept than is. `:113-114` ("IP addresses do appear in the server logs") also covers Render's own record of each request, whose fields were not checked, so that sentence stays until they are.

## Verified

**API pytest 5681 → 5688 (+7); the floor is raised to match. Web vitest unchanged at 2586.**

- **New:** in `test_logging_config.py`, `TestTheClientAddress`: the address is blanked and the rest of the line kept; a secret path is still redacted alongside; a record of another shape is untouched; through the filters `create_app` installs and **uvicorn's real `AccessFormatter`**, with the format uvicorn's default config gives it, the printed line carries no address; and `create_app` installs the filter once. In `test_dockerfile.py`, the line's `--ws none` and `--log-level info` asked of uvicorn's own parser, with `UVICORN_LOG_LEVEL=trace` set to show that the flag is what beats it. In `test_secrets_stay_out_of_logs.py`, **the real server**: uvicorn started with the words of the entrypoint's own `exec uvicorn` line, requests sent through `X-Forwarded-For` (an IPv4 and an IPv6 visitor) plus a WebSocket handshake to a token path, and every line the process wrote read back. The access line for `GET /api/v1/health` is there; neither address nor the token appears anywhere; no access line carries any address.
- **On this tree,** each file restored and its bytes checked after:
  - the address filter not installed: 3 of the 166 tests in `test_logging_config.py`, `test_secrets_stay_out_of_logs.py` and `test_dockerfile.py` fail, the real server's among them.
  - `--ws none` removed from the entrypoint: 2 fail (the real server's handshake line, and the parser's).
  - `--log-level info` removed: 2 fail (the parser's, which shows the variable then decides, and the real server's flag check).
- **security-reviewer: no blocker.** Taken: the WebSocket line and the `/privacy` note's reach (both above); the `UVICORN_LOG_LEVEL` pin; and the test's robustness (its flags now come from the entrypoint's own line, it adds an IPv6 visitor and a handshake, uses a Redis db of its own, and kills the server if it does not stop). Checked clean by the review: both of uvicorn's HTTP code paths log the same five arguments; the filter replaces a record's arguments and never touches the request, so rate limiting is untouched; no structlog event of ours carries an address.
- **Negative controls on the real server:** with the filter not installed, the test fails and the line reads `203.0.113.9:0 - "GET /api/v1/health HTTP/1.1" 200`; with `--ws none` removed, it fails on the handshake line quoted above.
- **The rest of the bar** (this tree, one run, 23:21 to 23:28):
  - Counts: API 5688, workers 27, shared-types 53 (0 fail), design-system 967, web 2586, mypy 42 (ceiling 50).

# The report's opening line names its biggest gap, with that dimension's own figure, instead of describing the score's band

**2026-10-09; branch `pilot-fixes-8`, item A2 of the founder's brief of 2026-10-08, the sentences approved by the founder on 2026-10-09.** The report narrative (Python and TypeScript), so the PDF and the web report alike, and one shared test table.

**Render: nothing to set.**

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 3, Insight (the finding a reader acts on first); lifecycle phase: Activation (Epic 9).

## 1. What was wrong

The score beat's heading came from the composite's band alone. RMIT University's re-run (composite 72.48) read "RMIT University shows up, but not reliably enough to be the default." — with a Mention Rate of 97.22. Its real gap is Share of Voice: named almost always, alongside rivals who take most of the mentions. The line described the wrong thing.

## 2. What changed

The line now comes from the biggest-gap dimension — the one the ledger and the gap beat already name, by the same tie rule — stated with that dimension's own whole-number figure. The founder's sentences, verbatim:

| Case | The line |
|---|---|
| failed / not scored / not enough data | unchanged |
| composite rounds to 0 | "{S} did not appear in any answer we measured." (unchanged) |
| Mention Rate | "{S} is missing from {100−m}% of unprompted answers." |
| Share of Voice | "{S} is named in {m}% of unprompted answers, but rivals take {100−s}% of the mentions." |
| Citation Strength | "When unprompted answers name {S}, they cite weaker sources than when they name {R}." |
| Sentiment | "{S} is named, but not consistently described favourably." |
| Technical Foundation | "{S}’s biggest gap is its own site, which scores {t} out of 100 on the technical checks." |
| nothing left to recover | "{S} is one of the names these answers reach for." |

RMIT University now reads **"RMIT University is named in 97% of unprompted answers, but rivals take 70% of the mentions."** Share of Voice counts presence, not which brand an answer recommends first, so "rarely the main pick" was not used.

**Where a sentence could not be made true, the line falls back to the band line every report used before** (no new copy):
- **A score from before v2.** A report renders a stored score under its own formula version, and Mention Rate and Share of Voice were first measured on unprompted answers in v2.
- **Citation Strength before v5, or with no rival strictly ahead.** v5 made it the authority of the sources cited per answer that names a brand; `{R}` is the rival with the highest Citation Strength, the first in the list on a tie. Help Scout's own v1.1 fixture has Citation Strength as its biggest gap with Zendesk tied, where the sentence would have been false.
- **A figure that would round to a false 0 or 100** (found by the UI review): a Share of Voice of 99.6 is not "rivals take 0%", and a Mention Rate of 0.4 is not "missing from 100%". An exact 0 or 100 is printed.

Every production score is v5 or later, so production reports always get the founder's sentences. `100 − s` uses the printed `s`, so the two percentages agree. The new narrative fields `formula_version` / `formulaVersion` and `top_citation_rival` / `topCitationRival` carry what the line needs.

## Found, not fixed

- **No floor on how large the gap is** (the UI review's second should-fix, a wording call for the founder). A Sentiment of 97 as the biggest gap reads "not consistently described favourably": true, since at least one answer was not positive, but strong for 97 out of 100. A Technical Foundation of 97 reads "its own site, which scores 97 out of 100". Both are the approved wording; a floor of about 2 points, below which the "reach for" line is used, is the cheap option if the founder wants one.
- The apostrophe in "{S}’s" is the typographic one, as every report string uses; the PDF's font draws it (WinAnsi 0o222).

## Verified

**API pytest 5691 → 5706 (+15); web vitest 2588 → 2602 (+14). Both floors are raised to match.**

- **New: one table, `packages/shared-types/fixtures/opening-lines.json`, read by both `test_report_narrative.py` and `derive.test.ts`,** so the PDF and the web are held to the same sentence. It has 14 cases, each built on Help Scout's payload with its version, composite, sub-scores and rivals' Citation Strength replaced:

  - each dimension as the biggest gap;
  - Citation Strength with two rivals tied (the first is named), with none ahead (the band line), and before v5 (the band line);
  - nothing left;
  - a v1.1 score (the band line);
  - a composite rounding to 0;
  - the four rounding edges: Share of Voice 99.6, Mention Rate 0.4, Mention Rate exactly 0, and Technical Foundation 0.4.
  A further Python test checks that the table covers every sentence.
- **The UI review: no blocker.** Taken: the rounding edges, and a redundant guard. Left to the founder: the floor above.
- **On this tree,** each file restored and its bytes checked after:

# A site with a brand's name under another country's suffix is proposed as that brand's other site, and the agency can confirm or dismiss it; nothing counts a confirmed site yet

**2026-10-09; branch `m1-other-sites`, market scope M1 task 1.1 (the founder's brief of 2026-10-09; the plan is `docs/plans/market-scope.md` on `market-scope-plan`).** The rule, three lists on two tables, one migration, two routes, and the contracts.

**Render: nothing to set.** Migration `89403ce44352` runs before the API serves. It adds three columns with a constant default, so no row is rewritten and nothing is backfilled.

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 3, Insight (which cited domains count as whose); lifecycle phase: Activation (Epic 9), the report an agency hands over.

## 1. What was wrong

A cited domain counts as the client's own only when it is exactly the client's domain (`extraction.classify_citation`). RMIT University's report counted `rmit.edu.vn`, RMIT Vietnam's site, as an independent source (four citations, the founder's brief of 2026-10-09). Because an `edu` domain is Tier A (`domain_authority`), the brand's own Vietnamese site raised RMIT's own Citation Strength. Nothing in the schema could say that a domain belongs to a brand other than its one `domain` column.

The plan, accepted as written on 2026-10-09: a domain with the brand's name under **another** public suffix is **proposed** as the brand's other site, and it counts as the brand's own only once the **agency confirms** it. This task builds the rule, the lists and the routes. **A proposal changes nothing, and so far nothing reads a confirmed site either:** task 1.2 makes the scan and the score use the confirmed lists, and task 1.3 the report.

## 2. What changed

- **The rule.** `other_sites.same_brand_elsewhere(domain, brand_domain)` holds when the label left of each public suffix is the same and not empty, and the suffixes differ. The split is `crawl.name_and_icann_suffix`, new beside `registrable_domain` with `name_and_suffix`, and read by the same extractor (the bundled Public Suffix List), so a domain is split exactly as every cited domain was reduced. Pinned cases: `rmit.edu.vn` for `rmit.edu.au` and `monash.edu.my` for `monash.edu` hold; `rmit-online.com`, `pineapple.com.vn` for `apple.com.au`, the brand's own domain (the same suffix is not "elsewhere"), an empty string, an IP address and `localhost` do not. **Only a suffix from the list's ICANN section counts** (the founder's decision of 2026-10-09): an address on a service anyone can sign up to, such as `rmit.github.io`, `rmit.blogspot.com` or `rmit.vercel.app`, is never proposed or accepted, and a brand whose own domain is such an address has no other sites. `registrable_domain` still reads the whole list, private section included. Both domains are compared in their DNS form (`intake.dns_form`: lower-case ASCII, each non-ASCII label IDNA-encoded, as the competitor editor already compares a rival with the client), so one host in two spellings is one host: `пример.xn--p1ai` is not another site of `пример.рф`, and `bücher.at` is one of `xn--bcher-kva.de`'s.
- **Proposals** come from the client's latest finished scan: succeeded or partial, with at least one answered result, newest first. Citations are counted per domain over the answered results only. A domain is proposed for the client first, else for the first rival in rank order that the rule fits; never a brand's own domain, and never one already confirmed or dismissed. They are sorted most-cited first, and each keeps the spelling the engine cited. Each brand's domain is split once, not once per cited domain. Working them out writes nothing.
- **Three lists**, each a JSONB array of registrable domains in the DNS form, NOT NULL with default `[]`. An ASCII domain is stored exactly as it is cited; `bücher.at` is stored as `xn--bcher-kva.at`, so a list holds one entry per host and only ASCII, whatever the database's encoding:
  - `clients.other_sites`: the client's confirmed other sites.
  - `clients.dismissed_other_sites`: domains the agency said are not any brand's own. There is one list per client, covering the client and its rivals, and a dismissed domain is never proposed again.
  - `competitors.other_sites`: a rival's confirmed sites, **on its row**. A scan's rival set is a frozen copy of the client's list, so a rival's sites have to be frozen with it.
- **Carried wherever rival rows are rewritten** (`services/competitors.py`):
  - `_copy_rows` copies a rival's sites into each new list, as a list of its own.
  - The competitor editor's replacement keeps them on a reused row, and clears them when the rival moves to another host or loses its domain (they were confirmed against the old one). Re-saving the same host in its other spelling keeps them.
  - Detection keeps them on a rival it finds again at the same domain, and clears them when it finds the same rival under another domain.
  - A new rival starts with none.
- **Two routes**, open to any member of the agency, as the competitors list is. Another agency's client gets the same `404` as an unknown one.
  - `GET /clients/{clientId}/other-sites` reads and writes nothing. It returns `confirmed` (the client's sites, then each active rival's on the list the next scan will use), `proposals` and `dismissed`.
  - `PUT` replaces all three lists and answers with the GET body. A rival's sites are written to the client's **next list**, made as a copy of the latest scan's set when there is none, through the competitor PUT's own helper (renamed from `_next_list_to_replace` to `next_list_to_replace`, now shared). A scan that has started keeps its own set. A save that changes no rival's sites makes no list.
  - **What the PUT refuses** (`422`, one plain sentence that names the domain, in `detail` and `errors[0]`): an entry that is not a bare domain (checked by `intake.rival_domain`, as a typed rival is; its sentence quotes nothing typed); more than 20 sites for one brand or 200 dismissed; a rival that is not active on the list, or is named twice; a site that is a brand's own domain, is an address on a service anyone can sign up to (`shared_hosting`), is not the brand's name under another suffix, or is confirmed for two brands; a domain both confirmed and dismissed. Nothing is written when any of these is refused. Every comparison is on the DNS form. **The caps count entries as sent and are checked before any site is read** (found by the security review): a request at the caps costs at most 430 domains of work, where one with 1,000-entry lists could make about 12,000 before its refusal. The request's schema bounds each list at 1,000 entries and the rivals at 10.
  - **`409` while the client's most recent scan is running**, with nothing written: the competitors list's own rule.
  - A save logs `other_sites.saved` with the client's id and three counts, and never a domain.
- **A rival cannot sit on a confirmed site's domain** (the founder's decision of 2026-10-09):
  - The competitor editor (`PUT /clients/{clientId}/competitors`) refuses a rival whose domain is confirmed as the client's other site, or as another kept rival's, with "rmit.edu.vn is confirmed as RMIT University's other site. Remove it there first." (`422`, `confirmed_other_site`, on that row's domain field, which the editor already shows beside the row's name). Nothing is written.
  - Detection skips such a candidate and logs `competitors.skipped reason=confirmed_other_site` with the client's id and the domain.
- **Contracts:** `docs/api-contracts.md` documents both routes, their errors and the carry rules. Its header gives the exported count, 54 paths and 64 operations; it still read 49 and 57, a count from before four paths and five operations that `main` already serves. `openapi.json` and `api.gen.ts` are regenerated: one path, two operations and five schemas are added, and nothing else changes.
- **One name, kept from the brief:** the plan names the module `siblings.py`. It is `other_sites.py`, the word its columns and its route use.

## Found, not fixed

- **No screen yet in this commit.** The confirmation card on the client's Sources tab, approved by the founder on 2026-10-09, is this branch's last commit. Until it lands, a site is confirmed through the API only.
- **Two saves at once can leave a rival on a confirmed site** (a nit of the second security review). The competitor save checks the client's confirmed sites before it locks the next list, and the other-sites save locks nothing when only the client's lists change, so the two run at the same moment can each pass its check. Task 1.2's precedence rule decides such a citation (a brand's main domain wins). The fix is to lock the client's row at the start of both saves.
- **A struck rival keeps its confirmed sites** (the same review's other nit), and gets them back when it is named again at the same host, even if one of them was confirmed for another brand meanwhile. Task 1.2's precedence rule then decides which brand a citation of it belongs to. The fix is to clear a rival's sites when it is struck, or to refuse the save that would carry a site another brand now holds.
- **The client's own domain is still matched exactly.** A cited domain keeps the spelling the engine gave, so a client at `bücher.de` whose site is cited as `xn--bcher-kva.de` is a third party to itself, as before M1. Only the other-sites lists are compared in the DNS form (task 1.2); changing the main-domain match is out of M1.

## Verified

  - `test_other_sites.py` (163): the split, including how the list splits a punycode suffix; the rule's table both ways round and in both spellings, with the founder's cases (`rmit.github.io`, `rmit.blogspot.com` and `rmit.vercel.app` never; `rmit.edu.vn` and `monash.edu.my` yes); the proposals (whose they are, rank order, never a brand's own domain, never confirmed or dismissed, the order, inputs left alone); and the PUT's validation, including the caps counted as sent and checked before any site is read (a counting wrapper shows only the rival domains are normalised first).

# A confirmed other site is the brand's own: RMIT University's rmit.edu.vn no longer adds to RMIT's Citation Strength, from the next scan, under v8

**2026-10-09; branch `m1-other-sites`, market scope M1 task 1.2 (the founder's brief of 2026-10-09).** Extraction, the scan runner, ad-hoc prompt runs, scoring, Tier B, and the scoring spec.

**Render: nothing to set.** No migration, setting or endpoint. Scans that start after the deploy are matched and scored under `v8`; every stored scan keeps its score, and an explicit re-score of a scan matched before `v8` is refused (pilot-fixes-8 A6's guard).

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 3, Insight (which cited domains count as whose); lifecycle phase: Activation (Epic 9).

## 1. What was wrong

Task 1.1 (`8324a8f`) gave the agency a way to confirm `rmit.edu.vn` as RMIT University's other site, but nothing read the confirmed lists: a citation still counted as the client's own only on exact equality of domain, so RMIT's own Vietnamese site (Tier A, `edu`) stayed an independent source and raised RMIT's own Citation Strength.

## 2. What changed

- **Who a cited domain belongs to** (`extraction.classify_citation`, `extract_facts`), in this order: the subject's domain, then a rival's domain, then the subject's confirmed other sites, then a rival's. **A brand's main domain wins over any confirmed site** (the security review of 1.1), for the case where a rival is later placed on a domain another brand had confirmed. The two main-domain comparisons stay exact strings, as before; the two other-sites comparisons use the cited domain's DNS form (`intake.dns_form`, cached), since the lists are stored in it and a cited domain keeps the engine's spelling. Brand matching (`find_brand`) is untouched: a confirmed site never makes a mention.
- **`MATCHER_VERSION` → `v8`**: it versions what a scan stores from an answer, which since v8 includes which brand a cited domain belongs to. **`FORMULA_VERSION` → `v8`**: an input change (who a cited domain belongs to); weights, tiers, exclusions and formulas are untouched. `docs/scoring-spec.md` has the v8 row and says what "its own" means where Citation Strength is defined.
- **The list is read once.** `scan_runner.run_scan` reads the client's confirmed sites at the RUNNING stamp, and the rivals' from the scan's own frozen set, and every answer of the run is typed by those. Nothing downstream reads the client's list again: the report, the CSV, the fix generator, scoring and an explicit re-score read what the scan stored (`cites_subject` per citation; the rivals' sites on the scan's own rows). An ad-hoc prompt run reads the lists once, at its own moment. A later edit of the list therefore never re-types a stored scan (a test edits the list after a scan and checks the stored rows, the digest, Citation Strength and the report are unchanged).
- **A rival's confirmed site is linked to that rival** (`_competitor_id_map`: every rival's name and domain first, then the rivals' other sites with `setdefault`; the lookup falls back to the DNS form only after the exact one misses), and the rival's own credit leaves it out (`scoring.answer_authority`: `d != domain and dns_form(d) not in other_sites`).
- **The inputs digest** adds a rival's `otherSites` only when it has some, so a rival without any serialises exactly as before: with the version string set back to `v7`, a fixture gives the digest captured from the code before this change.
- **Tier B** (`domain_authority.market_participants`) also refuses a live client's and any competitor's confirmed sites, as it refuses their main domains: `rmit.edu.vn` is RMIT's own whoever cites it.
- **The fix generator needs no change.** A confirmed site the scan cited is already among the cited domains a fix may name; one the scan did not cite stays out under launch checklist 3.95 (generated fixes name only cited sites). Tests pin both.
- **The unclaimed list** (the report's "Get onto …" source) needs no change either: a client's confirmed site is stored as citing the client, and a rival's is linked to the rival, so neither can be unclaimed. A test through a real scan pins it.
- Words written in 1.1 that said nothing read the lists yet now say what does, in the code, `docs/api-contracts.md` (which also says the explicit re-score now refuses a scan matched before v8) and the docstring of migration `89403ce44352`, which has not shipped; none of its operations changed.

## Found, not fixed

- **Tier B compares the stored DNS form with the domain as cited**, in SQL, so a sibling cited only in its Unicode spelling is not refused there. Tier B needs a domain to be frequent across the whole platform, so this is accepted and stated in its docstring.
- **RMIT University's stored scans keep their scores**, with rmit.edu.vn counted as an independent source in them: scoring never re-scores history, and their explicit re-score is refused. The first scan after the agency confirms rmit.edu.vn is the first to count it as RMIT's own.

## Verified

**API pytest 6082 → 6110 (+28); the floor is raised to match. Web vitest unchanged at 2604.**

- **The founder's pair, first and red:** an answer naming RMIT University (rmit.edu.au) and citing only rmit.edu.vn, at Tier A, through `extract_facts` into `scoring.answer_authority`. Run on the code before the change it gave `cites_subject` False and a credit of exactly `Decimal("100")`. Now: with rmit.edu.vn **confirmed**, `cites_subject` True and a credit of exactly `Decimal("0")`; with it only **proposed**, False and exactly `Decimal("100")`, today's figure. With a second Tier A source in the same answer: 100 confirmed against 200 proposed.
- **New (28):**
  - `test_other_sites_attribution.py` (25): the founder's pair and the second source; Monash's confirmed site linked to Monash and left out of its credit; the Unicode spelling; the precedence order; the rival map; the digest pin and the digest's change when a rival has an other site; both versions at `v8`; Tier B refusing a client's and a rival's confirmed site, and not a deleted client's; the fix generator allowing a cited confirmed site and refusing an uncited one; a real scan with stubbed engines storing `cites_subject` True and matcher `v8` for the confirmed site, with neither site unclaimed nor in a fix; a later edit of the list changing nothing stored; a `v7` scan's explicit re-score refused.
  - `test_prompt_run_other_sites.py` (3): an ad-hoc run stores a confirmed client site as the client's own and a confirmed rival site as the rival's (failing first, as `False` and `other`), and a site only proposed as before.
- **Version pins moved, and only the version:** `test_scoring.py` (both constants), `test_robots_obeyed.py` (three asserts and its three pinned digests, re-pinned; with the version set back to `v7` the code gives the old pins), `test_failed_audit_reason.py`, `test_score_endpoints.py` and `test_scan_chain.py` (the constant instead of a literal). Migration `5863629b56ab` and `test_scan_matcher_version.py`'s literals, which are history, are untouched.
- **On this tree,** each file restored and its bytes checked after:
  - the client's confirmed sites ignored by `classify_citation`: 6 of the 196 tests in `test_other_sites_attribution.py`, `test_prompt_run_other_sites.py`, `test_domain_authority.py` and `test_scoring.py` fail.
  - the rival exclusion back to its main domain only: 2 fail.
  - Tier B not refusing confirmed sites: 2 fail.
  - the scan reading no confirmed list: 1 fails.
  - an ad-hoc prompt run reading no confirmed list: 1 fails.
  - the digest dropping a rival's other sites: 1 fails.
  - a rival's other site overwriting a main domain in the rival map: 1 fails.
- **The rest of the bar** (this tree, one run, 15:07 to 15:14):
  - Counts: API 6110, workers 27, shared-types 53 (0 fail), design-system 968, web 2604, mypy 42 (ceiling 50).
  - All six count gates pass through `assert_count.py`.
  - Ruff is clean, all typechecks pass, and the styleguide builds.
  - Both `uv lock --check` runs pass, and Alembic upgrade and check pass on an empty database.
  - The Python licence audits pass in both environments, and the JavaScript audit passes (`pnpm licenses list --json`).
  - OpenAPI and `api.gen.ts` regenerate to exactly the committed files.
- Exit codes were read from files.

# The report names a brand's confirmed other sites under its evidence ("RMIT University's other sites: rmit.edu.vn — 4 citations"), and the CSV attributes them to the brand

**2026-10-09; branch `m1-other-sites`, market scope M1 task 1.3 (the founder's brief of 2026-10-09).** The report API, the CSV, the PDF and the web report.

**Render: nothing to set.** The report gains one field; no migration, setting or host. A report built from a scan before v8 reads exactly as it did.

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 5, Presentation (the report a client reads, on screen, as a PDF and as a CSV); lifecycle phase: Activation (Epic 9).

## 1. What was wrong

After task 1.2 (`a366d3e`), a citation of a confirmed other site is stored as the client's own, but the report had nowhere to say so: the evidence beat's own-sources table would have listed `rmit.edu.vn` as if it were the client's main site, with nothing to tell a reader why, and the founder asked for the line "RMIT University's other sites: rmit.edu.vn — 4 citations" under the evidence beat.

## 2. What changed

- **The API splits the client's own cited domains in two** (`services/report.py`, `ReportProofOut`): `subjectCitedDomains` keeps the client's own domain, compared exactly as `extraction.classify_citation` compares it, and the new **`subjectOtherSites`** holds every other domain stored as citing the client, most cited first, then by domain. `subjectCitations`, the total, is unchanged: confirmed sites are the client's own pages. A scan from before v8 has no such domain, so its report is unchanged (a test).
- **The line**, the same sentence on the web and the PDF, under the own-sources table: "RMIT University's other sites: rmit.edu.vn — 4 citations". Several sites are joined by "; " in the API's order, one is "1 citation", and nothing prints when there are none. `report_narrative.other_sites_line` and `derive.ts`'s `otherSitesLine` are twins, held to one table of cases (`packages/shared-types/fixtures/other-sites-lines.json`). The PDF draws it through the writer's own text call, so its keep-together rules apply.
- **The own-sources table's empty message stays true.** "No answer cited RMIT University's own pages." would be false when a confirmed site was cited but the client's own domain was not, since that site is one of its own pages and the paragraph above counts it. In exactly that case the message is "No answer cited rmit.edu.au." (the client's domain, which the report already carries); when both lists are empty, the web and the PDF keep their messages as they were. One pair of twins, `own_pages_empty_message` and `ownPagesEmptyMessage`, on the same table of cases.
- **The CSV** lists the client's own domain, then its other sites, then everything else, so `rmit.edu.vn` reads `Attributed to: RMIT University` by the existing rule; a rival's confirmed site reads the rival's name (1.2 links it to the rival).
- Contracts: `docs/api-contracts.md` documents the field; `openapi.json` and `api.gen.ts` gain it and nothing else. The shared-types report cases and the web report fixtures carry `subjectOtherSites: []`.

## Found, not fixed

- **The line is tied to its table only by position** (the ui-reviewer). It follows the table in the reading order on the web, but a screen-reader user moving table by table does not meet it. Tying it with `aria-describedby` needs a new prop on the design system's table; left for now.
- **The new empty message is Claude's wording**, made because the old one would have been false; the founder may want other words.
- **A client stored with `www.`** (before launch checklist 3.67) is compared as stored, exactly as the extractor compares it, so its own domain stays in the own-sources table only in that spelling.

## Verified

**API pytest 6110 → 6129 (+19); web vitest 2604 → 2617 (+13). Both floors are raised to match.**

- **On this tree,** each file restored and its bytes checked after:

# The client's Sources tab has a "Sites with the same name" card: the agency confirms or dismisses each proposed site for the client and its rivals, and removes a confirmed one

**2026-10-09; branch `m1-other-sites`, market scope M1, the confirmation screen (the founder's approval of 2026-10-09).** The web app only.

**Render: nothing to set.** No API change; the card calls the two routes task 1.1 added (`8324a8f`), through the web's same-origin `/api/v1`.

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 5, Presentation (the agency's client workspace); lifecycle phase: Activation (Epic 9), where the founder confirms rmit.edu.vn for RMIT University after the deploy.

## 1. What was wrong

Tasks 1.1 to 1.3 (`8324a8f`, `a366d3e`, `ff88b28`) built the rule, the lists, the attribution and the report, but a site could be confirmed only by calling the API. The founder approved the smallest screen on 2026-10-09 and asked for it inside M1, so they can confirm rmit.edu.vn on it after the deploy.

**2026-10-09; branch `m1-other-sites`, launch checklist 3.111 (2), the founder's decision of 2026-10-09.** The web app only.

**Render: nothing to set.** No API change: `PUT /clients/{clientId}/other-sites` already replaces the dismissed list.

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 5, Presentation (the agency's client workspace); lifecycle phase: Activation (Epic 9).

## 1. What was wrong

The approved card (`b4683fb`) listed no dismissed sites, so a site marked **Not theirs** by mistake could be taken back only through the API. The founder's words: "a collapsed 'Dismissed (n)' list under the card, each with Undo (removes it from dismissed; it's proposed again)".

## 2. What changed

- **The list.** When anything is dismissed, the card ends with a toggle, **Dismissed (n)**, collapsed by default: a design-system `Button` (quiet, small) with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, the pattern of the shell's own nav disclosure. Expanded, each dismissed domain has **Undo** (its accessible name "Undo: rmit.com.au"). Undo sends the save without that domain and with everything else as it was (`otherSitesBody`, a fourth action), and says "rmit.com.au can be suggested again." It does not claim the domain is listed: it is proposed again only if the latest finished scan cited it, which the API decides. The toggle disappears with the last dismissed site; the status line takes the focus.
- **Hidden means hidden.** The collapsed list is a plain `div` with `hidden`, and the flex list sits inside it. Tailwind 3.4's preflight hides `[hidden]` at the same specificity as `.flex` and earlier in the sheet, so `<ul hidden class="flex">` would have shown while "collapsed" in a browser, which jsdom cannot see. A test pins that the controlled element carries no display class, and the production-build screenshots below show the list hidden.

# A scan's questions are never mostly template filler: the templates read as real questions placed in the client's country, or the prompt phase fails visibly; the CSV says how many questions came from each

**2026-10-09; branch `f5-prompt-fallback`, F5 of the founder's brief of 2026-10-09 (part A; the root cause of the short set is part B).** The prompt generator, the scan runner and executor, the report API, the CSV and one web sentence.

**Render: nothing to set.** No migration, setting or host. From the deploy, a scan whose questions cannot be written ends `failed` with `PROMPTS_UNAVAILABLE` instead of running on templates, and is not counted against the agency's scans.

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 2, Measurement (the questions a scan asks), with Layer 1, Delivery, for the CSV row that reports it; lifecycle phase: Activation (Epic 9).

## 1. What was wrong

RMIT University's second scan of 2026-10-09 asked about half its questions from `prompts.fallback_prompts`: "who are the best providers of university", "what are the most recommended university companies", "how much does university cost". The templates pasted the industry label into sentences written for service businesses, with no market, and nothing recorded how many of a scan's questions they wrote. Two more faults in the same path:

- **One long question sank the whole set.** The SDK strips JSON-schema constraints the API does not support, the 300-character limit among them, and checks them after the answer arrives, so one generated question over the limit failed the whole response and the scan ran on templates alone.
- **A generator failure scanned on 11 templates** and counted as a scan.

## 2. What changed

- **Templates are true sentences, or there are none** (`fallback_prompts`). They exist only when the client has both a category noun (its `industry` label: one to four words, not a placeholder such as "other" or "business") and a market read from its domain's country-code ending, from the same 14 endings detection searches by (`MARKET_BY_TLD`, pinned to `serp.SEARCH_COUNTRY_BY_TLD`'s keys). A domain whose ending names no country (`.com`, `.org`, `.io`, `rmit.edu.vn`'s `.vn`) has none: detection's Australian default is a search setting, not a fact about the client. For RMIT University the nine read: "what is the best university in australia", "which university is best in australia", "how do i choose the right university in australia", "what matters most when choosing the right university in australia", "what are the best alternatives to RMIT University in australia", "how does RMIT University compare with other university options in australia", "is RMIT University a good choice in australia", "how much does RMIT University cost", "what should i know before choosing RMIT University". Each is pinned for a count noun ("university"), a person noun ("dentist") and a mass noun ("customer service software").
- **Templates only ever top up.** The generator's questions are kept when it writes 20; when it writes 15 to 19 the set is topped up to 20 from the templates if there are any, and otherwise stays at the generator's count; when it writes fewer than 15, or fails (timeout, API error, unusable answer), **the scan fails before any engine is asked**: `failed`, `errorCode: "PROMPTS_UNAVAILABLE"`, not counted against the agency's scans (`scan_allowance`: a failed scan never counts). The web says: "The questions for this scan could not be written, so nothing was asked. Run the scan again. It does not use up one of your scans."
- **One bad question is dropped, not the set.** The model's schema carries no length limit; questions over 300 characters, and blank ones, are dropped one by one and counted.
- **Counted, logged and shown.** `build_prompt_set` logs `prompts.generated` (scan id, questions kept, questions dropped) and, only when templates were used, `prompts.fallback_used` (scan id, count, reason); a failed prompt phase logs `prompts.unavailable` with its reason (`generation_failed`, `schema_violation`, `unusable_answer`, `too_few_questions`). The counts are stored on the prompt set (`fromGenerator`, `fromFallback`, in its existing JSON), the report API carries them as `promptOrigin` (agency report only; `null` on a shared report and for a scan stored before), and the CSV's Scan section has two new rows, "Questions written by the generator" and "Questions from templates", with "Not recorded" for an older scan.
- Contracts: `docs/api-contracts.md` (the new error code, `promptOrigin`, the five Scan rows); `openapi.json` and `api.gen.ts` gain the one field.

## Found, not fixed

- **Why the generator came up short is part B.** Two causes fit the code: Opus returned a valid but short list (the old top-up path), or the call failed and the scan ran on all 11 templates (two 60-second timeouts with Opus 5 thinking by default, the 8,000-token cap shared with that thinking, or one over-long question). The scan's `llm.call … purpose=prompt_generation` and `prompts.` log lines decide it; they are in Render's logs, which this machine cannot read.
- **The dedicated `except PromptsUnavailable` in the executor only sets the log level** (a warning, not a traceback). The failure code is decided by `_failure_code`, which the end-to-end test pins; removing the clause leaves the tests green, by design.
- **An invalid `intent` in the model's answer still fails the whole response** (now as `schema_violation`, a visible failure). Structured outputs enforce the enum, so it should not occur.
- **A failed prompt phase is paid for and free to repeat** (the security review's should-fix; a decision for the founder). It costs the generator's call (and, on a client's first scan, the detection before it) and never counts against the agency's scans, and nothing limits how often a scan is started, so a client whose site steered the generator into failing could be re-scanned at our cost without end (unconfirmed that a site can steer it that reliably). Before this change the same failure scanned on templates and counted. The fix is a limit: count such failures after a few a day per agency, or rate-limit scan starts; a limit is the founder's call.
- **A city is not read** from a domain; the country is the market until market scope (M2) lands.

## Verified

**API pytest 6129 → 6196 (+67); web vitest 2661 → 2662 (+1). Both floors are raised to match.**

- **New:** `test_prompt_fallback.py` (65): the nine templates as whole strings for "university" at rmit.edu.au (the founder's regression case), "dentist" and "customer service software"; each of the 14 market phrases, and the table pinned to detection's; no templates for a domain with no country ending (rmit.com, zendesk.com, acme.org, acme.io, rmit.edu.vn), a placeholder label or a long one; the generator returning 20, 17 (with and without a market), 15 and 10, a timeout and an API error; an over-long and a blank question among 20; the log lines and stored counts through `build_prompt_set`; a scan failing end to end through `execute_scan` (`failed`, `PROMPTS_UNAVAILABLE`, no engine called, not counted); and the stored counts after a `promptLimit` cut (17 + 3 cut to 6 stores 6 and 0; cut to 18 stores 17 and 1). The CSV endpoint test reads the two rows; `scanOutcome.test.ts` the new sentence; existing tests updated for the new return type and the five Scan rows.
- **On this tree,** each file restored and its bytes checked after (`test_prompt_fallback.py`, `test_report_csv_endpoint.py` and `test_facts_only.py` hold 223 tests):
  - templates allowed with no market: 12 fail.
  - no floor of fifteen: 3 fail.
  - over-long questions kept: 3 fail.
  - the CSV row for templates dropped: 5 fail.
  - the template count not stored: 5 fail.
  - the counts taken before a `promptLimit` cut: 1 fails.
  - the failure-code mapping without `PROMPTS_UNAVAILABLE`: 1 of the 65 in `test_prompt_fallback.py` fails (removing only the executor's own `except` clause fails nothing, as above).
- **security-reviewer: no blocker.** Taken: the stored counts are worked out from the set actually asked (a `promptLimit` cut them after counting), a verification script that unpacked the old return pair, and a comment that said the failure "spends nothing". Its should-fix, the cost of a free failure, is under Found, not fixed, for the founder. Checked clean: no new log line or stored detail carries a generated question, a secret, a token or an email; `promptOrigin` is `null` on the shared report and its PDF and read only under the agency's own scan; the new failure leaves no scan running, no claim or lease held, and never counts; parsing without the length limit stays bounded by the call's token cap.
- **ui-reviewer: no blocker, no should-fix.** The sentence is true (a failed scan never counts), matches the other failure sentences, never shows the code, and renders through the same two places (the dashboard and the report), neither a live region, as every other; the shared report never shows it. Its one nit, that this is the only failure sentence with an instruction ("Run the scan again."), it recommends keeping.
- **The first full bar was red** (12 API tests, 1 web), all tests that encoded the old behaviour or guard the report's shape, none weakened: the guard that every number in the report is classified now classifies the two counts; the CSV tests expect five Scan rows and know the two labels; the share-link test leaves `promptOrigin` out of its byte comparison, as it leaves `scanErrorCode`; a usage test about every engine refusing now keeps the generator answering, so it still reaches the engines (a refused generator now ends the scan before them, which `test_prompt_fallback.py` pins); and a stubbed request in the new tests used a `.invalid` address, which the web's guard against placeholder addresses anywhere in `apps/` caught.
- **The rest of the bar** (this tree, one run, 19:28 to 19:37):
  - Counts: API 6196, workers 27, shared-types 53 (0 fail), design-system 968, web 2662, mypy 42 (ceiling 50).
  - All six count gates pass through `assert_count.py`.
  - Ruff is clean, all typechecks pass, and the styleguide builds.
  - Both `uv lock --check` runs pass, and Alembic upgrade and check pass on an empty database.
  - The Python licence audits pass in both environments, and the JavaScript audit passes (`pnpm licenses list --json`).
  - OpenAPI and `api.gen.ts` regenerate to exactly the committed files (they changed with this item: one field).
- No live provider call was made: every model call in these tests is stubbed.
- Exit codes were read from files.

# The question generator's call states its thinking setting, survives two transient failures instead of one, and logs the HTTP status when it fails

**2026-10-09; branch `f5-prompt-fallback`, F5 of the founder's brief of 2026-10-09 (part B: the cause; part A is `5f96ada`).** The prompt generator's call and its bound, and the scan deadline's arithmetic.

**Render: nothing to set.** The generator's call can now take up to 182 s instead of 122 s before it gives up; a normal call takes about 12 s.

Drift check (north-star §8): Layer 2, Measurement (the call that writes a scan's questions); lifecycle phase: Activation (Epic 9).

## 1. What was wrong

RMIT University's second scan of 2026-10-09 ran on template questions. Production's logs could not be read from here, so the call was reproduced live (the founder approved up to US$1; US$0.17 was spent): seven calls shaped exactly like production's for RMIT University (rmit.edu.au, industry "university", five rivals), each a single attempt with a long timeout.

- **Every call was healthy:** exactly 20 questions (10/7/3 or 9/8/3 by intent), `stop_reason` `end_turn`, 690–757 output tokens, 0 thinking tokens under Opus 5's default (adaptive, effort medium), 10.8–13.6 s, no question over 300 characters. Two of them with thinking explicitly off were identical (20 questions, 696 and 751 tokens, 11–14 s).
- So in normal conditions the 60-second limit has about five times its use, the 8,000-token cap about ten times, and nothing is over-long. None of the three suspected causes occurs; what remains is a **failed call**: a timeout, or an overloaded or erroring answer, on both of its two attempts. The scan then fell back to all 11 old templates (six name RMIT and read passably, five are the nonsense the founder quoted), which part A now refuses to scan.
- The production scan was not confirmed: its log lines are in Render, and the question count (11 for a fallback) would confirm it.

## 2. What changed

- **Thinking is set explicitly:** `thinking={"type": "disabled"}`, beside effort `medium` and `max_tokens` 8,000. Claude Opus 5 has no thinking token budget (`budget_tokens` is refused with a 400), so "off" is the explicit form; the measurements show the model used none here anyway, and the questions were the same with it off.
- **Three attempts, not two:** `GENERATOR_BOUND` is 60 s × 3 (ceiling 182 s). The SDK retries timeouts, 408/409/429/5xx and overloaded answers with backoff.
- **The cause is logged:** `prompts.generation_failed` carries the error's class and, for an API status error, the HTTP status (`status=529`); never any response text.
- **The scan deadline still holds:** its comment now reads a worst case of 2,124.5 s of 2,400 s (slack 275.5 s, margin ×1.13, was 2,064.5 s and ×1.16), on the stated assumption that every call in a scan times out at its ceiling; the deadline is unchanged. The stale "measured at 14.6 s" note is replaced by the measurement above.

## Found, not fixed

- **The cause in production is inferred, not read:** the scan's `llm.call … purpose=prompt_generation` and `prompts.` lines would settle it, and from this deploy a failure names its HTTP status.
